**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P1. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment an operator could configure a cleartext http outbound destination and PHI would cross the network unencrypted, with a warning at most. This is the highest-consequence cell in this batch.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external facing, HTTP-based services, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications."

**What holds it short today.** The inbound half is genuinely strong and should not be re-graded downward: `check_http_tls_exposure` raises a `WiringError` on a non-loopback bind without TLS, and `_inbound_insecure_bind_permitted` clamps the escape so that `serve --allow-insecure-bind` does not permit the bind on the assessed enforcing PHI posture -- a gate that refuses to start. Outbound is where it goes. The exposed-gate family in `wiring_runner.py` is inbound-only, `check_egress_allowed` is a host allowlist rather than a TLS requirement so an allowlisted http host is permitted, and the one outbound refusal, `refuse_cleartext_credential_hop`, keys on a named credential riding the hop -- a PHI body with no Authorization header never reaches it.

**The research question.** What refusal would close the outbound half without breaking the hops it legitimately permits -- loopback, and the per-connection `tls_hop_attested` claim for a proxy-terminated or trusted-segment hop? Named unknowns: whether "this destination will carry PHI" is decidable at construction time at all (the credential gate is decidable because a credential is declared; a body is not), and whether an operator attestation is sufficient evidence for an L1 pass or is exactly the compensating-control-on-a-claim shape the method discounts. Prior to both, and load-bearing: the scorecard records an unsettled narrow-versus-broad reading over whether V12.2 reaches the engine acting as a client, resolved today only by the worse-verdict tie-breaker.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** An owner ruling adopting the narrow section reading. It moves the cell to pass with no code change, and the scorecard supplies the tell itself: it notes the same finding is also carried by 12.3.1, so nothing about the exposure would have changed -- only which cell carries it.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 43 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as zero occurrences of the cell id across `docs/BACKLOG.md` and the closed archive). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. Reachable with a build -- and this item's central sentence is FALSE in the shipped code, as is the same sentence in the record it was filed against.** The item says "the one outbound refusal, `refuse_cleartext_credential_hop`, keys on a named credential riding the hop -- a PHI body with no Authorization header never reaches it." A second, body-keyed outbound refusal ships: `refuse_cleartext_egress` at `messagefoundry/transports/rest.py:547`, whose own docstring opens by naming this requirement and says it exists because a cleartext outbound "puts the PHI-bearing request body on the wire even with no `Authorization` header". It is wired unconditionally into all four HTTP-family destinations and the FHIR read path (`rest.py:1232`, `soap.py:377`, `fhir.py:331`, `fhir.py:842`, `dicomweb.py:246`), each with a comment naming the requirement, plus a zero-I/O send-time re-assertion at `rest.py:381` called from five delivery sites. Measured by execution under the assessed posture: a bare `http://partner.example.org` REST, SOAP, FHIR or DICOMweb destination raises `InsecureHopRefused` at construction, with the matching loopback destination CONSTRUCTING as the positive control in the same run. **It was present at the cell's own verification commit**, so the drift is in the RECORD and not only in the item -- and a security record asserting that a shipped fail-closed refusal does not exist under-claims a control operators would otherwise configure around.

**Two of the item's three named unknowns are retired by shipped code.** Whether "this destination will carry PHI" is decidable at construction is moot: the deciding parameter was deleted from the authority (`config/tls_policy.py:520-525`), and the engine refuses every non-loopback cleartext HTTP-family egress regardless of body -- executed and confirmed on a PHI non-enforcing posture and on a non-PHI enforcing posture, because a shipped-strict floor turns a non-enforcing warning back into a refusal. And whether an operator attestation is sufficient evidence is moot on this cell, because `tls_hop_attested` is UNREACHABLE from every supported authoring surface: `inspect.signature` over the code-first factories shows no such parameter and no `**kwargs` escape, and a `connections.toml` load raises both as a top-level key and under `[settings]`, with the sibling `cleartext_accepted` key LOADING successfully as the positive control in the same run. That makes the inbound gate an UNCONDITIONAL refusal on the assessed posture -- stronger than the record says.

**What actually holds the cell short is smaller and different: in-scope CLIENT surfaces whose refusals key on "a credential would cross" rather than on "connectivity", which is what the verb ranges over -- and there are five of them, not three.** `ide/src/engineTarget.ts:58-69` `assertTargetAllowed` is a real refusal with no escape, but it is applied per call site, and re-running the gate-coverage scan with the same positive control (seven files contain the gate) returns eight request sites and FIVE ungated, not one. Worse, a SECOND and deliberately weaker gate exists that no prior pass opened: `ide/src/engineTarget.ts:82` `assertBrowsableUrl` screens the scheme allow-list and DROPS the cleartext-off-box check, with its docstring saying why -- "That gate refuses cleartext off-box because CREDENTIALS would cross the wire; merely opening a console page sends none". Its two non-test callers are `ide/src/statusBar.ts:770` (open web console) and `ide/src/auth.ts:66` inside the sign-in fix path, so on an off-box `http://` engine setting the extension would hand the OS browser a cleartext origin and, on the second path, send the operator there for password rotation and MFA enrolment. The in-code rationale permitting that is a premise this cell would have to overturn, and its own "sends none" clause does not hold for the credential-management destination. Because all five paths derive from `messagefoundry.engineUrl` (`ide/src/cli.ts:83-85`, no validator), validating that setting at read is the PRIMARY fix, not an optional extra.

**And the inbound limb carries a reachable relaxation the record does not grade.** `[api].tls_terminated_upstream` (`config/settings.py:803`) unlocks a non-loopback bind through `exposure_protected` at `:837`; the only load-time constraint is a non-empty `trusted_proxies` at `:962-963`, with no requirement that the bind be loopback. The settings file states the consequence in its own words at `:805-807` -- "the proxy to engine hop is a plaintext segment on the internal network" -- holds it with two operator attestations, and says of them "They are NOT runtime enforcement." That is an attestation-held cleartext inbound hop on the assessed enforcing-PHI posture, of exactly the shape the outbound analysis grades. It matters for the shape of the answer: under the NARROW section reading limbs A and C decide the cell, so adopting that reading is not merely unnecessary but INSUFFICIENT, and the tempting sentence "limb A is already a pass at HEAD" is not established.

**Still not an honest pass:** the item's named trap holds -- an owner ruling adopting the narrow reading moves the cell with no code change, and the record supplies its own tell, since the same exposure is carried by 12.3.1. But it is no longer the tempting move; the tempting move now is the opposite, re-scoring to pass on the newly-found outbound refusal alone, which grades the inbound and outbound limbs and silently drops the client limb -- "covers only part of the in-scope surface" verbatim. Nor declaring the IDE's tokenless probes out of scope because they carry no credential (the verb says all connectivity, not all credentialed connectivity, and the poll fires every fifteen seconds against whatever the setting names). Nor making `cleartext_accepted` refuse under enforcement and calling that the fix: defensible product work, but it touches neither the client limb nor the fallback limb, and it would remove raw TCP and X12 from off-loopback use on every enforcing instance until the unbuilt raw-transport TLS work lands -- buying the cell with the product's purpose. Nor citing `check_egress_allowed`, a host-and-port allowlist blind to scheme, which cannot express the requirement at all. Proposed work, unallocated and by subject: validating the IDE engine-URL setting at read; promoting the IDE target gate from a credential gate to a connectivity gate across the status-bar probe, its poll and read-environment callers and the AI-policy read, with a distinct rendered state so a refusal does not render as an outage; naming and overturning the browsable-URL gate's documented rationale so the two external-launch sites stop handing the OS browser a cleartext off-box origin; refusing rather than degrading a non-loopback cleartext tray engine URL, and explicitly NOT adding an https-then-http probe, which would create the fallback this cell forbids; deleting the apiclient non-loopback warn-and-cross escape (zero deployments, so the removal costs nothing) and updating the two load-harness call sites; adding a scheme gate to the two Vault client constructions, routed through the one authority AND its refusal floor rather than the bare authority, which only warns on a non-enforcing instance; a limb-A decision on the upstream-termination relaxation -- record it in the residual or close it by requiring a loopback bind when TLS terminates upstream; retiring the residual's false outbound sentence and re-anchoring onto the outbound refusal and its call sites; and correcting the off-loopback deployment note that tells operators the cleartext-egress refusal is PHI-posture gated, measured false at HEAD where it refuses on every posture.

## 1178. research an honest pass for ASVS 12.3.1 -- what a no-fallback claim means under the owner-ratified cleartext gradient

> 🔢 **Re-scored 2026-08-20 -> P2.** Value **7/10** · Difficulty **4/10** · _quick win_. Both limbs re-read at HEAD and both hold: transports/tcp.py:150-152 and transports/x12.py:124-125 declare cleartext_accepted a PERMANENT, STRUCTURAL declaration with no tls parameter to migrate to, and config/tls_policy.py:503-519 documents the loopback, hop_attested, cleartext_accepted and not-enforcing arms ahead of REFUSE. Value 7 because a first deployment would put a raw-TCP or X12 partner hop on the wire in the clear with no in-product configuration that changes it; difficulty 4 because this item's own remainder is the reading against the ADR 0153 gradient plus an owner ruling, with the connector TLS build tracked at #311. _(was 7/10 · 5/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **12.3.1** (L2) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb requires an encrypted protocol on every inbound and outbound connection and forbids falling back to an unencrypted one. Two limbs fail: raw TCP and X12 cannot speak TLS in any configuration, and the shared hop decision ships four ALLOW/WARN arms ahead of its REFUSE.
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment a raw-TCP or X12 partner hop would cross the network in cleartext with no configuration that changes it, and an operator could cross any other cleartext hop under a logged, audited `cleartext_accepted` declaration.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols."

**What holds it short today.** Re-read at 166634c9: `transports/tcp.py:150-152` and `transports/x12.py:125` both state that for these connectors `cleartext_accepted` is "a PERMANENT, STRUCTURAL declaration ... there is no `tls = true` to migrate to" -- no `tls` parameter, no `ssl` import (BACKLOG #311 tracks the connector work). And `config/tls_policy.py:501-515` documents the shared decision's explicit precedence: loopback allows, `hop_attested` allows, `cleartext_accepted` warns, not-enforcing warns, and only then refuse. That gradient is owner-ratified under ADR 0153. This cell's residual is dated 2026-08-01 at `f8d11685`; both anchors were re-read for this item and still hold.

**The research question.** The ADR 0153 gradient is an owner ruling -- the research must ask what an honest pass looks like under it, not propose removing it. The verb says the server must not fall back, and a WARN arm that crosses a cleartext hop is a fall-back on its face, so the question is whether any of the four arms can be reconciled with the verb: loopback plausibly is not a network hop at all, and an attestation is a claim that the hop is encrypted elsewhere, but `cleartext_accepted` is the hard one. Separately: can raw TCP and X12 carry TLS against the partners that actually use them -- X12 counterparties typically ride a VAN or AS2 rather than a bare socket -- or is the honest finding that these two connectors put an L2 pass permanently out of reach?

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Citing the `cleartext_accepted` audit trail as the compensating control. It is a record that the hop is unencrypted, not a control that encrypts it, and the verb is about the protocol rather than the paperwork. Re-verifying against the loopback default and calling the exposure hypothetical is the other move -- the default posture is not the assessed one.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 43 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as zero occurrences of the cell id across `docs/BACKLOG.md` and the closed archive). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. This needs an OWNER RULING on one question the record itself frames and declines, and this item's severity sentence is wrong in its second half in a way that changes what a build must do.** The item says a raw-TCP or X12 partner hop "would cross the network in cleartext with no configuration that changes it". Measured at HEAD `79fdfe2b` on the assessed posture, the shipped code REFUSES that hop rather than crossing it: `TcpDestination` and `X12Destination` capture an `InsecureHopGuard` (`transports/tcp.py:143`, `transports/x12.py:117`) and enforce at construction, `config/tls_policy.py:539` returns REFUSE on an enforcing, non-loopback, unattested, unaccepted hop, and that raise propagates out of `runner.build_check(registry)` at `pipeline/engine.py:1590` -- before any start. Inbound, `check_tcp_tls_exposure` (`pipeline/wiring_runner.py:7045`) raises at `:7075` unless `_inbound_insecure_bind_permitted` returns true, and that helper's production-PHI clamp at `:6747` makes `--allow-insecure-bind` inert. The hop crosses only under a per-connection `tls_hop_attested` or `cleartext_accepted`. "No configuration changes it" is true of the PROTOCOL and false of the OUTCOME, and a signed relaxation is a different defect from an ungated default -- the rubric names them separately.

**The item's citation of the connector work is CORRECT and a prior research pass measured it false.** That pass grepped only the engine clone and concluded the citations at `transports/tcp.py:152` and `transports/x12.py:125` dangle. The ledgers are partitioned at `scripts/hooks/ledger_check.py:105` (`PUBLIC_BACKLOG_FLOOR = 1000`), so the low number lives in the vault ledger, where it resolves at a heading reading "TLS for raw TCP and X12 transports", open since 2026-07-25, scoped as net-new transport work plus the certificate and verification settings the other transports already expose, with adjacent numbers resolving as controls. That pass's instrument could not have returned a hit whatever was true. **The load-bearing build IS tracked, the shipped citations resolve, and the prior pass's "re-file under a properly allocated number" item should be struck.**

**Answering the item's own question, which decides everything downstream:** the loopback arm reconciles with the verb (an on-box hop puts no byte on a network, and `is_loopback_hop_host` is structural -- it never resolves DNS, so a name resolving to loopback is still treated as remote), but it cannot carry this cell, because the assessed posture is off-loopback on both planes by construction. The attestation arm reconciles only under one of its two meanings: `transports/mllp.py:156` defines it as "the hop IS secure by means the engine cannot see", which is delegation for a proxy-terminated hop and segmentation for a trusted-segment one, and one boolean carries both with no code able to tell them apart. The acceptance and not-enforcing arms do not reconcile under any reading -- the verb's first sentence requires that an encrypted protocol IS USED, and a WARN that crosses the hop means it was not. So the honest pass shape is forced: every hop must speak an encrypted protocol or REFUSE, with no expressible per-hop relaxation.

**The inventory that ruling would range over is incomplete, and the missing artifact is one the verb's enumeration names in terms.** `messagefoundry/transports/database.py` -- simultaneously an outbound destination, an inbound `DatabasePoll` source and the hot-path `DatabaseLookupExecutor` behind the ADR 0010 carve-out -- appears nowhere in the analysis. On `dialect='generic'` it is not merely gated-with-an-escape but UNGATED: `_build_connection` returns `weakened=False` unconditionally at `database.py:403`, which disarms the byte-crossing tripwire `_assert_send_hop` (defined `:129`, called `:692`), and the only control is `_warn_generic_tls_unenforced`, whose own docstring at `:345-354` concedes "a generic PHI connection with no TLS keyword would cross in plaintext with no refusal and no trace" and states "This is advisory only; it never gates or changes the connection." Every reporting surface it feeds is non-blocking. That is the shipped-default limb, not a signed relaxation, and it is this item's own named trap -- a record that the hop is unencrypted rather than a control that encrypts it -- in a module nobody opened. Two more consequences: `database.py:108-109` places `if attested: return True` AHEAD of the posture clamp at `:110-113`, a second instance of the pattern the ruling-free fix corrects one file over; and the guarded condition at `:158` is `(trust or not encrypt)`, so `tls_hop_attested=true` there permits an outright plaintext ODBC session (`Encrypt=no` emitted at `:199`), not merely verify-off.

**Still not an honest pass:** the item's two traps hold -- citing the acceptance audit trail as the compensating control fails because the shipped sink exists precisely to distinguish an accepted cleartext hop from one that merely warned, and re-verifying against the loopback default is MORE decisive now because the assessed posture is off-loopback on both planes. The most tempting move is not in the item: point at the shipped refusals -- every piece of which is true and re-confirmed -- and claim the startup-refusal limb is satisfied. It fails on the rubric's other sentence in the same row, that a signed relaxation is never a pass, and the per-feed escapes are authorable per connection. Two more: for the SMB and backup hops, arguing the payload is already encrypted is the paperwork trap in cryptographic clothing (encrypting the cargo removes exposure and does not turn an unencrypted protocol into an encrypted one); and for the reachability probe, "it sends zero bytes so nothing is disclosed" is the vacuity argument in miniature, bought purely to avoid a one-parameter change. Proposed work, unallocated and by subject: TLS on the four bare asyncio calls in the raw-socket connectors (already tracked -- do not re-file); the gradient amendment retiring the crossing arms and the standalone attestation, owner-gated; moving the attested early return behind the production-PHI clamp at BOTH sites, the inbound bind helper and the DATABASE weakened-TLS predicate; re-scoping the attestation retirement across every consumer of that flag rather than only the shared authority; refusing a generic-dialect DATABASE hop under an enforcing PHI posture when the advisory predicate returns a reason, and making the corresponding check required rather than advisory; replacing the off-box upstream-termination allow at `__main__.py:1646` with a verifiable requirement; a scheme gate on the three Vault hops and routing the insecure-LDAP escape through the posture clamp; passing the destination's SSL context into `probe_tcp_reachable` (`transports/base.py:557`) so a `tls=true` MLLP destination's connection test does not open a plaintext socket to the partner, and grading the second bare connection in `verify/smoke.py:126`; moving the IDE target gate into its client and dropping the payload-keyed exemption; wiring the four inbound exposure checks into the offline build-check path, measured NOT shipped; and a correction pass over the prior salvaged research entry striking its untracked-citation drift point.


**OWNER RULING 2026-08-22 -- build the data-layer gate, and rule the partner-feed question separately.** The re-scoping found **14 data-layer hop sites across 11 shipped modules**, of which **8 reach no TLS gate of any family**; they are cleartext by default or by absence, not by a signed per-connection relaxation. So this cell stays partial on the data-layer limb *even if every clinical partner feed is ruled out of scope* -- the interop question the packet posed can no longer dispose of the cell. The ruling has a second half that is about the record rather than the build: recording a permanent partial and attributing it to clinical interop would be **a true sentence about the wrong cause**, which is the compensating-control-on-a-false-premise defect the standards forbid. The gate work is owed on its own merits; the partner-feed scope question is still open and is now genuinely separable.

**Built 2026-09-03 under that ruling: the generic-dialect DATABASE hop is gated. One of the 8 ungated data-layer sites, and the item's own named one.** `transports/database.py` on `dialect='generic'` reached no TLS gate of any family: `_build_connection` returned `weakened=False` unconditionally, which also disarmed the `_assert_send_hop` tripwire, and the SQL Server preset's refusal never runs on that path -- so the only control was `_warn_generic_tls_unenforced`, a log line whose own docstring conceded the hop would cross in plaintext with no refusal and no trace. A deploying site would have put a DB hop on the wire in the clear with no per-connection declaration behind it. The arm now goes through the SAME shared authority every other cleartext transport consumes (`InsecureHopGuard` -> `insecure_hop_disposition`), captured exactly as `TcpDestination`/`X12Destination` capture it: refused at construction, so it fails `messagefoundry check` / dry-run / reload / the `serve` pre-flight before any start, with a zero-I/O re-assertion at the byte crossing. Both the outbound destination and the inbound `DatabasePoll` are gated -- the poll link dials out on the same hop with the same credential in the same DSN. It can only refuse or warn where the shipped code was silent, so ADR 0092 decision 5 (no-loosen) holds by construction, and the ADR 0153 gradient itself is untouched.

**Scope held deliberately narrow, and three things are measured-and-unclosed.** (1) The SQL Server preset keeps its own posture-keyed weakened-TLS refusal; moving that arm onto this gradient would ADD the loopback and `cleartext_accepted` relaxations to a path that refuses today, which is a loosening. (2) The `database.py` attested-before-the-clamp ordering stands: the clamp it precedes is the global `MEFOR_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS` escape, so per-connection-attestation-then-clamped-escape is the ratified precedence, and moving it would retire the attestation arm on this cell -- which is the owner-gated question, not this build. (3) The `(trust or not encrypt)` condition still lets `tls_hop_attested=true` emit an outright plaintext `Encrypt=no` ODBC session rather than only verify-off. Narrowing it would make the module's two dialects disagree about what an attestation licenses, since the shared gradient's arm 2 lets an attestation ALLOW a cleartext hop everywhere else. It belongs to the item's own "re-scoping the attestation retirement across every consumer of that flag", which is owner-gated. The remaining data-layer sites and the partner-feed scope question are both untouched, so the cell does not rescore on this alone.

## 1179. research an honest pass for ASVS 12.3.3 -- internal-hop transport encryption when a certificate cannot be a shipped default

> 🚧 **IN PROGRESS 2026-08-22 -- builder-1 lane**, banner written by the dispatcher: `BUILDER.md` puts banner flips outside a builder's lane and the lane-versus-broadcast expiry is ambiguous enough that two builders read it differently, so this seat writes it. > Research: done 2026-08-20

Difficulty 5: a scoping ruling, a one-line Dockerfile change and a bounded startup check that can sit on the existing exposure_protected property without colliding with the revocation refusal. _(was 7/10 · 7/10.)_

> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **12.3.3** (L2) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb asks that transport encryption cover all connectivity between internal HTTP-based services, with no fallback to unencrypted communication. Every first-party internal hop defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8765` because `tls_cert_file: str | None = None` at `messagefoundry/config/settings.py:712`, and the shipped image carries a genuine downgrade at `docker/Dockerfile:91` (both re-read at 166634c9).
> **SHIPPED-BUT-OPEN 2026-08-22 -- PR #512, ledger pairing authored by the LANDER per [ADR 0165](adr/0165-a-builder-pr-satisfies-the-ledger-gate-with-a-paired-commit-authored-by-the-dispatcher-or-lander.md).** The RIPE defect shipped: `make_self_signed` wrapped every SAN in `DNSName`, IP literals included, so a minted certificate verified against none of the three first-party clients that default to `127.0.0.1:8765`. Fixed at BOTH coupled sites -- `read_cert_facts` read `DNSName` only, so a writer-only fix would have left the cert inventory under-reporting exactly the certs the writer creates.
> **NOT A CLOSURE, and the remainder is NOT RIPE rather than merely unfinished.** The zero IDE CA seam is verified absent (0 of 108 TypeScript files, control fires) and stays open deliberately: nothing mints a CA yet, so the seam would point at nothing. The banner is untouched here -- it is set by a separate in-flight ledger PR, and writing it twice is how one item ends up carrying two states.
>
> **RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 at `2b8bccb43`, BY EXECUTION, AND THE PREMISE MOVED AGAIN. The 2026-08-20 research warned in capitals that A RULING IS NOT A CONTROL. The control has since landed, so that warning is now spent and quoting it as if it still stood would be the error it existed to prevent.** [ADR 0172](adr/0172-the-engine-always-serves-tls-minting-a-self-signed-certificate-on-first-run.md) was accepted 2026-08-22 and part A shipped as PR 575 under [#1276](#1276-generate-a-self-signed-tls-certificate-on-first-run-when-no-certificate-is-configured). Running the shipped code on a default `ApiSettings()`: `ensure_api_tls_material` ([`api/tls.py:87`](../messagefoundry/api/tls.py)) mints `api-generated-cert.pem` + `api-generated-key.pem` beside the store, `build_api_ssl_context` accepts them, and `__main__.py:2884-2901` hands the context to `uvicorn.run` through `ssl_context_factory`. **So the engine's end of every first-party internal hop is https on the shipped default, and the encryption limb is BUILT for the in-process bind.** A second call returns the same pair rather than re-minting.
> **WHICH OF THIS ITEM'S EVIDENCE LINES SURVIVED, measured one at a time.** Still true: `[api].tls_cert_file` ships `None` and `tls_enabled` is still literally `bool(self.tls_cert_file)` (`config/settings.py:765`, `:845-847`); all three first-party client defaults are still cleartext loopback (`ide/src/cli.ts:84`, `tray/config.py:37`, and `apiclient/client.py:237` -- **the client anchor this item carried as `:188` is off by 49 lines**, so locate it by the `base_url: str = "http://` phrase); `proxy_intra_service_auth` still ships `"none"`. **Falsified: the INFERENCE those lines carried.** `tls_enabled is False` no longer means "the engine opens a cleartext socket" -- it now means only "the operator supplied no certificate", and the mint runs precisely in that state. Any reader of this item who treats `tls_cert_file: None` as evidence of a cleartext bind is reading a predicate that changed meaning underneath the anchor. **Also confirmed landed, not assumed:** the IP-SAN fix is real at both coupled sites -- a minted certificate's SANs read back as `['127.0.0.1']` through `read_cert_facts`, which now reads `IPAddress` as well as `DNSName` (`pki.py:200-213`, `:180-190`).
> **THE DOWNGRADE LIMB SHIPPED FIXED IN THIS PASS, and it is the only limb that ever failed on a shipped artifact.** `docker/Dockerfile:91` carried the two-arm probe byte-for-byte until this change; it is now a single https arm, `curl -fsS -k "https://127.0.0.1:${MEFOR_API_PORT:-8765}/health" || exit 1`, with the cleartext fallback deleted. **The port question the proposed work said to decide BEFORE the build has an answer and it is not a constant:** the engine's shipped default is `8765`, while `docker/compose.yaml` and both `docker/k8s/*.yaml` move it to `8443` via `MEFOR_API_PORT`, which is the only expression of the port the image can read at probe time. So the probe reads that variable and falls back to the live engine default, and `tests/test_container_health_probe.py` pins the fallback to `ApiSettings().port` by import rather than by copy. Every predicate in that file is mutation-proved against the pre-fix probe held verbatim as a positive control. **Keep the item's own caveat: `/health` is tokenless and carries no PHI, so this is a downgrade-limb fix and not a PHI exposure fix.** `-k` deliberately stays: it skips verification on a hop inside the container's own network namespace, it does not skip encryption, and it cannot reach a cleartext socket -- the deleted second arm could.
> **THE SHARDED PROVISIONING QUESTION IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN OPEN-ENDED, AND IT IS STILL A DECISION NOBODY HERE MAY TAKE.** The exclusive-create loser's "unspecified outcome" is specified: reproduced directly, a second caller against a state directory that already holds `api-generated-key.pem` raises `FileExistsError` out of `_write_private_key` (`__main__.py:3487-3499`), and nothing on the serve path catches it (the two `except FileExistsError` handlers at `:3558` and `:3713` are both in the `cert` CLI verbs), so that shard subprocess exits and the supervisor's restart finds the completed pair on the next attempt. The N shards also derive the SAME `state_dir`, because it is `Path(settings.store.path).resolve().parent` and `supervisor.py` varies only the file stem, so today's accidental answer is ONE shared certificate -- which happens to be right, since the minted identity is `[api].host` and every shard shares it while differing only by port. **Accidental is not decided**; the one-shared-versus-one-per-shard choice, the loser's intended outcome and the client pin belong to [#1276](#1276-generate-a-self-signed-tls-certificate-on-first-run-when-no-certificate-is-configured) part B, where they are recorded. Not re-filed, per this item's own instruction.
> **WHAT STILL HOLDS THIS CELL SHORT, unchanged by any of the above.** The `tls_terminated_upstream` hop is plaintext BY DESIGN and ADR 0172 excludes it deliberately, so the hop this cell scores is exactly the one the mint does not cover. The three client defaults still dial `http` at an https listener, which writes a request line and its bearer token as plaintext bytes into a TLS socket the engine cannot parse: the connection fails, so the practical effect is a broken client rather than a working cleartext channel, and on shipped defaults those bytes never leave loopback. The IDE certificate-authority seam is still absent and still deliberately open. None of that is this pass's to close, and **this item cannot be closed by a builder at all** -- the closing act is a scorecard re-score.
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** REDUCED 2026-09-03, and by a landed control rather than a re-reading. ADR 0172 makes the engine terminate TLS on the shipped default, so "cleartext unless the operator configured TLS at both ends" no longer describes the engine's end of an internal hop; the container probe's cleartext fallback is deleted. What remains would still bite a first deployment. The `tls_terminated_upstream` proxy hop is plaintext by design and is exactly the hop this cell scores. The tray, `apiclient` and the IDE still default to `http`, so each writes a request line and its bearer token as plaintext bytes into a TLS socket before the connection fails, which is a broken client rather than a working cleartext channel, and on shipped defaults those bytes stay on loopback.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism used for all connectivity between internal, HTTP-based services within the application, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications."

**What holds it short today.** The residual grades six internal HTTP hops and finds the engine's own end of each cleartext on shipped defaults, with no gate that refuses to start when a hop lacks TLS. The downgrade limb fails on a shipped artifact: the HEALTHCHECK is `curl -fsS -k https://127.0.0.1:8443/health || curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8765/health || exit 1`, verification disabled on the TLS arm and an unconditional cleartext fallback. The k8s manifests are clean by contrast, so this was a Docker-path choice. **BOTH SENTENCES ABOVE ARE SUPERSEDED 2026-09-03 and "today" in this heading now means 2026-08-08 -- see the re-measurement in the banner.** The engine's own end of the in-process bind is https on shipped defaults (ADR 0172), and the probe quoted here no longer exists in the tree. The quoted text is kept verbatim because it is the positive control `tests/test_container_health_probe.py` mutates every predicate against.

**The research question.** The `tls_cert_file` default is classified deliberate: the engine refuses off-loopback in-process TLS because it performs no certificate revocation check, and a private key and certificate cannot be shipped values. So the question is what an honest pass requires when the vendor cannot ship the material the control needs. Three named unknowns: whether "internal HTTP services" can honestly exclude loopback hops, since the requirement text carries no loopback carve-out and the engine's design does; whether a startup gate could refuse a non-loopback internal hop lacking TLS without colliding with the revocation refusal already in the tree; and whether the proxy-to-engine hop is a product control at all or a deployment topology the assessment must record as out of scope, and who decides that.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Giving `proxy_intra_service_auth` an `"mtls"` default: nothing in the tree branches on that value (see 12.3.5), so the declaration changes no byte on the wire. Removing the Dockerfile fallback arm alone: it closes the downgrade limb and leaves the encryption limb exactly where it was, so it cannot be the pass on its own. Re-declaring loopback hops out of scope to shrink the hop set is a scope move, not a finding.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. Reachable with a build -- and this item's research question was OVERTAKEN by two owner acts it predates, while its evidence is accurate in every particular.** Re-measured at HEAD `79fdfe2b`: `[api].tls_cert_file` still ships `None` (`config/settings.py:758`, and `tls_enabled` at `:831` is literally that setting), `proxy_intra_service_auth` still ships `"none"` (`:817`), all three first-party client defaults are still cleartext loopback (`ide/src/cli.ts:84`, `messagefoundry/tray/config.py:37`, `messagefoundry/apiclient/client.py:188`), and `docker/Dockerfile:91` still carries the downgrade byte-for-byte. What changed is the QUESTION. The item asks what an honest pass requires when the vendor cannot ship the material the control needs; its premise (a private key cannot be a shipped value) stands, and the conclusion drawn from it -- therefore TLS cannot be a shipped default -- was answered twice after filing, and the answer is **mint the material rather than ship it**: a 2026-08-16 owner filing authorising the override of the five shipped DEV-ONLY prohibitions, and a 2026-08-17 ruling plus same-day amendment warning on loopback and REFUSING to serve a non-loopback bind until a real certificate is configured, reasoned in the assessment rubric's own terms. Separately, the rubric itself got stricter after filing: an off-by-default control can never be graded pass, and a warning is not a refusal -- which forecloses scoring the opt-in certificate path.

**The item's second named unknown is settled negatively and cheaply.** `in_process_tls_revocation_refused` (`config/tls_policy.py:275-303`) returns false for a loopback bind, a plaintext bind, a proxy-terminated bind and an attested bind, firing only on an unproven off-loopback in-process TLS bind, so the amendment's refusal and the revocation refusal COMPOSE rather than collide. What is genuinely unsettled is a consequence the amendment does not address: the sanctioned escape from the revocation gate is a declared terminating proxy, and `tls_policy.py:286-288` describes that escape in its own words as "the engine then runs plaintext behind it and terminates no TLS itself" -- which is exactly the hop this cell scores.

**The structural argument that makes the build work is right in shape and over-stated in scope, and the correction changes the build.** `uvicorn.run(` occurs exactly once in the engine (`__main__.py:2868`) with no redirector, and every internal HTTP hop terminates on it, so encrypting that socket encrypts all of them by construction. But that is a CALL-SITE count, not a SOCKET count. `serve --shards` is shipped and supported: `pipeline/supervisor.py` derives a deterministic specification per shard whose argv carries `--shard <id> --port <base+i>` and launches one subprocess each, and `pipeline/sharding.py:32-34` states it -- each shard gets "an independent API port (`<base>+offset`) so each shard's console/health endpoint is reachable". So a sharded deployment binds N listeners and three build questions fall out that the path never names: N subprocesses starting concurrently against one `O_EXCL` key path is a race with an unspecified outcome for the loser; the generated path must surface through the per-process `[api].tls_cert_file` (which `tray/config.py:206-219` reads to choose its scheme, so a certificate minted to an unnamed internal path leaves the tray dialling cleartext at an https listener and reporting a running engine as DOWN); and pinning "the generated CA" on each client does not say whose CA when there are N.

**Two more concrete defects must land inside the minting work.** `messagefoundry/pki.py:136-165` `make_self_signed` builds `SubjectAlternativeName([x509.DNSName(d) for d in dns_names])` -- DNS names only, zero IP-address entries -- so an IP-literal loopback URL would fail hostname verification against the engine's own certificate; the better fix is standardising every client default on a hostname, which also retires a separate identifier defect. And the IDE has no certificate-authority seam at all: zero hits for `rejectUnauthorized|ca:|NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS|createSecureContext` across all 108 TypeScript files under `ide/src`, with `minVersion` firing five times in the same run as the positive control, so an engine-minted certificate would be invisible to the extension and the environment-variable workaround is not product configuration. The five shipped DEV-ONLY strings (`pki.py:141-143` plus four CLI strings in `__main__.py`) must be REWRITTEN, not deleted, recording that the prohibition was overruled, by whom and when.

**Still not an honest pass:** the item's three traps hold, and the first is measured inert -- `proxy_intra_service_auth` occurs six times tree-wide, three of them inside message strings, and the only predicate asks whether it is non-"none" (positive control: a setting that IS branched on returns 14 hits in the same run), so an mTLS default would change no byte on any wire, and three of its four permitted values imply no encryption at all. Deleting the container fallback arm closes one limb and leaves the other where it was. Re-declaring loopback hops out of scope is the most dangerous single move available, because it would close BOTH limbs at once -- the encryption limb by shrinking the hop set and the downgrade limb by carrying a container-loopback probe out of scope with it -- and a subtler variant now exists, using the shipped-default rule to argue the proxy hop is out because the default is loopback; that rule governs whether an off-by-default CONTROL can pass and does not license shrinking the HOP INVENTORY. Three the item could not have named: landing the mint without the client work, which produces a pass on a product that does not work; flipping the Posture-B loopback warning at `__main__.py:1770-1777` to a refusal and calling it the startup limb, since it refuses on MISSING ATTESTATIONS rather than on cleartext, so an operator satisfies it by typing two strings and the hop stays plaintext; and **treating the 2026-08-16 filing and the 2026-08-17 ruling as if they were the control -- a RULING IS NOT A CONTROL**, the prohibition is still verbatim in the code, nothing in the serve path mints anything, and re-scoring on an authorised-but-unbuilt change is the purest form of the move the method exists to refuse. One cost stated plainly, because it is why this was declined once: a browser reaching the console over a freshly minted certificate gets a full-page trust interstitial until the certificate is imported, which trains an operator to click past a TLS warning on the interface engine's own console, and a certificate-error origin is not a secure context. The re-enrolment half of that cost is vacuous at zero deployments; the secure-context half is not, and it is the strongest remaining argument against the build. Proposed work, unallocated and by subject: mint-and-serve on first run (already filed by the owner as an open ledger item -- do not re-file, add these defects to its scope); IP-address entries in the minted certificate, or standardising client defaults on a hostname; a certificate provisioning story for a sharded deployment, with a stated outcome for the exclusive-create loser and an explicit one-shared-versus-one-per-shard decision; the off-loopback refusal implementing the amendment; an amendment recording the revocation gate's loopback exemption as a decision rather than the accident of a short-circuit; the IDE certificate-authority seam; the first-party client scheme migration with a pin seam added to the tray probe; the Posture-B runbook rewrite to an https upstream with verification on (measured zero occurrences of an https upstream directive in that 1742-line document today, against two plaintext ones as the control); collapsing the container health probe to a single arm on a port decided BEFORE the build; removing or clamping the apiclient plaintext escape and correcting the three harness hints that promise a fix the flag cannot deliver; and re-anchoring the cell's twelve drifted evidence lines against unique tokens, never by a mechanical offset.

## 1180. research an honest pass for ASVS 12.3.4 -- narrowing internal TLS trust when the anchor is an artifact only the deployer holds

> 🔢 **Re-scored 2026-08-20 -> P2.** Value **7/10** · Difficulty **6/10** · _big bet_. Both shortfalls confirmed at HEAD: the anchor ships off, and on the HTTP egress family it is inexpressible, since resolve_trust_anchor reaches only dicom, mllp and remotefile while rest.py and soap.py expose verify_tls alone and both hvac sites pass no CA. On a first deployment every internal REST, SOAP, FHIR, DICOMweb and Vault hop would verify against the whole OS store, including the hop that hands out the store data-encryption key. Difficulty 6 because this is a client-construction change across rest.py, soap.py and both hvac sites plus a refuse-versus-fall-back posture decision, not a default flip. _(was 7/10 · 6/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **12.3.4** (L2) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb asks that internal TLS use trusted certificates and, where internal or self-signed certificates are in play, that the consuming service trust only specific internal CAs. `trust_anchor_mode: TrustAnchorMode = "system"` at `messagefoundry/config/settings.py:969` with `internal_ca_file = None`, so internal-CA certificates are verified against the whole OS trust store.
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment an internal FHIR, REST, SOAP, DICOMweb or Vault hop would be verified against the full OS store, so any public CA that could be induced to mint a certificate for the internal hostname would be accepted on a hop the operator believes is anchored to their own PKI.

**The pinned verb.** "Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates."

**What holds it short today.** Two distinct shortfalls. The narrowing mechanism is real, exclusive and fail-closed where it exists (`resolve_trust_anchor` sets `load_system_roots=False` on a per-connection CA; `pinned` is refused at config load without an `internal_ca_file`), and it ships off. Separately, on the largest slice narrowing is not merely off but inexpressible: `resolve_trust_anchor` is never imported into `transports/rest.py` or `transports/soap.py`, so the whole HTTP egress family exposes only `verify_tls`, and `hvac.Client(url=addr, token=token)` gets no CA argument on the hop that hands out the store's data-encryption keys.

**The research question.** The 2026-08-08 shipped-default triage classifies this deliberate and puts it in the "flipping buys nothing" bucket -- the only confirmed member there -- because the exclusive posture requires an artifact only the deploying organisation holds. So: what does an honest pass look like for a requirement whose secure state depends on operator-supplied material? Unknowns to name: whether an engine-expressed anchor can reach the HTTP egress family at all given how those clients are constructed; whether an anchor-absent internal hop should refuse rather than fall back to the OS store, and on which posture that would be defensible; and whether a declared-internal-PKI attestation could be made load-bearing rather than decorative, given that 12.3.5 shows this product already carries an attestation nothing reads.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Shipping `trust_anchor_mode = "pinned"` as the default: the validator refuses without `internal_ca_file`, so every stock config would fail to load. And the move the residual itself names as the hostile attack -- arguing that a hospital's OS trust store is the enterprise CA, so `system` mode is already narrow. That is a property of the operator's image build laundered into a product control, and the method forbids it.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. CONTESTED -- the two adversarial passes refuted the finding on different grounds and recorded different answers, and the disagreement is exactly the funding question, so it is recorded as a decision owed rather than resolved.** Both stated shortfalls in this item hold at HEAD `79fdfe2b`, with the trust-mode anchor drifted (`trust_anchor_mode` is at `config/settings.py:1015`, not `:969`). One severity clause is wrong on one of its five named hops: the item says an internal Vault hop "would be verified against the full OS store". Both `hvac.Client(url=addr, token=token, allow_redirects=False)` sites (`config/secretprovider_vault.py:80`, `store/keyprovider_vault.py:97`) pass no CA argument, and hvac rides `requests`, whose default bundle is the PUBLIC roots -- not the OS store -- so an internal-CA Vault would FAIL CLOSED on a first deployment rather than be broadly trusted. The direction matters: the item overstates the trust breadth and understates a different defect, that the shipped Vault client cannot reach an internal-CA Vault at all.

**This item's third unknown is already answered in shipped code.** It asks whether a declared-internal-PKI attestation could be made load-bearing rather than decorative, given that 12.3.5 shows an attestation nothing reads. That dead one is a different flag. The per-hop transport attestation is a WORKING template: `config/tls_policy.py:533` returns an allow verdict on it, `config/models.py:196-205` refuses the flag without a mandatory reason, and `pipeline/wiring_runner.py:6220-6221` and `:6281-6282` read it per connection. So the answer is yes, and the pattern already ships.

**The inexpressible slice is real and is wider than measured.** The finding's factory probe ran over seven of the twenty-five uppercase connector factories in `config/wiring.py`. Re-run over the full set with `Soap()` (`:2564`, returning `client_cert_file` and `client_key_file`) as the positive control and five non-HTTP factories returning empty as the negative control, FOUR factories expose `bearer_token` and `basic_user` and NO certificate parameter: `Rest()` at `:1878`, `FHIR()` at `:1949`, `DICOMweb()` at `:2235` and `FhirLookup()` at `:494`. The lookup executor is not carried "for free" -- it is a distinct factory whose runtime class builds its own per-connection opener map at `transports/fhir.py:846-871`, separate from the destination construction at `:375-412`, and it is the sanctioned live read-only lookup against an internal FHIR server, which is the most on-point instance of the verb's condition in the product. `Ftp()` at `:2740` likewise exposes only `tls` and `tls_allow_expired`, so the per-connection pin that `transports/remotefile.py:217` already reads is unreachable from either authoring surface.

**The forcing control is where the two passes part, and both grounds reproduce.** The first pass showed a serve-time and build-check gate in the engine process CANNOT reach the IDE extension, a declared in-scope artifact -- a server cannot observe whether a client narrowed its trust anchor -- while the proposal nonetheless names an IDE certificate file among the anchors that gate would inspect; and that the Vault hop has neither the settings nor the posture handle the design assumes, because the provider builds its client per resolution from environment variables with no settings block in scope. The second pass showed the PRECEDENT that made the gate fundable without a ruling is a misreading. **Read at HEAD:** `forward_hop_disposition` (`config/settings.py:2512-2515`) returns ALLOW on its FIRST branch for verified TLS, with the in-code comment "an encrypted+authenticated hop, nothing to gate", and never inspects anchor breadth; it delegates to an authority whose docstring opens "Decide what to do with a **cleartext** transport hop", and `__main__.py:1471-1480` refuses only a hop that "is not a verified-TLS hop". The mandatory-CA property on that hop comes from a protocol-local validator at `config/settings.py:1490-1500`, inside an opted-into protocol with no OS-store default to fall back to. So the shipped ladder is a precedent for refusing an UNPROTECTED hop, while the proposed gate would refuse an UNNARROWED but verified-and-authenticated hop -- the state the shipped ladder ALLOWs by written decision. That is a NEW policy inverting a ratified one, so this item's second unknown is still open and is an owner call; zero deployments removes the migration cost of that policy but does not supply the ruling.

**The declaration arm should be demoted rather than central.** On every hop it covers, the resulting trust configuration would be byte-identical to today's `system` and `None` defaults, and the verdict would rest on an unverified operator assertion about a third party's issuer -- and `checks.py:1529` already records the pressure that shape creates, warning that blocking on a declared acceptance pushes operators toward a false attestation, for a gate far narrower than the one proposed. A measurable predicate is available on almost exactly the hops the expressibility work plumbs: validate the peer chain against a PUBLIC-ONLY bundle; if it validates, the verb's condition demonstrably does not obtain and no declaration is needed; if it does not, an internal or self-signed certificate is demonstrably in use and the specific anchor is required. `requests` takes a bundle path, so the Vault hop is measurable too; only the ODBC and Schannel hops are genuinely out of reach, and that is the honest place for a declaration and a named residual.

**Still not an honest pass:** the item's two traps hold -- shipping `trust_anchor_mode = "pinned"` as the default is refused at config load without an internal CA (`config/settings.py:1025-1031`) so every stock configuration would fail to start, and arguing that a hospital's OS trust store IS the enterprise CA is a property of the operator's image build laundered into a product control. The sharpest trap is a third the item does not name: the cell's own re-score trigger says to watch for the anchor resolver or a CA parameter appearing on those HTTP factories, so **the expressibility work trips that trigger by construction, and if it lands and the cell is re-scored while every default is still permissive, that is wiring an existing toolkit into the pipeline so an absence claim stops firing -- wearing the hat of a trigger the cell wrote for itself.** Expressibility must never be scored without the forcing control. Two more, both reachable from the record: re-scoring on the discovery that the generic ODBC dialect passes operator keywords through (a newly FOUND opt-in capability is not a newly BUILT control, and that dialect is not the default), and re-scoring on the syslog hop (one hop of roughly a dozen, reached only by opting into a non-default protocol). Proposed work, unallocated and by subject: the HTTP-egress trust-anchor threading across ALL FOUR factories that lack a certificate parameter, including the lookup executor's own opener map and the separate webhook opener; the Vault client CA argument and scheme gate, with the honest note that it needs new settings and a posture handle on a lazy environment-fed path rather than reusing the shipped ladder; the FTPS factory's lost CA and verification parameters; the DATABASE default-dialect server-certificate parity fix, which the store code already emits against the identical driver; the tray probe CA pin; the IDE certificate-authority setting AND a separate IDE-side forcing rule with its own publicly-certified-peer arm, since no engine-side gate can reach a separate process; the anchor-discipline posture gate, owner-gated and specified against a public-chain-probe predicate wherever measurement is possible with the declaration arm confined to the ODBC and Schannel hops; posture reporting of an unnarrowed internal hop as a first-class loosening; an explicit disposition for the augmenting trust mode, which keeps the OS roots and so does not satisfy the word ONLY; an ECH-sidecar egress ruling rather than leaving it in the unknowns while a pass is claimed; and extending the anchor-integrity preflight beyond the three auth-path anchors.

## 1181. research an honest pass for ASVS 12.3.5 -- intra-service endpoint authentication on an engine whose coordination is store-mediated

> 🔢 **Re-scored 2026-08-20 -> P2.** Value **6/10** · Difficulty **7/10** · _big bet_. The setting is still attestation-only: its sole consumer at settings.py:850 collapses four values to a boolean, so a declared "mtls" changes nothing. Value 6 rather than 7 because the hop the item's own severity names is genuinely closable today -- setting [api].tls_client_ca_file makes the API listener CERT_REQUIRED-verify the proxy's client cert (api/tls.py:58-62) -- so the gap is an unverified declaration beside a working control rather than an unavailable one; difficulty 7 because an honest pass must decide whether an attestation-only setting should exist at all, whether mutual PKI is reachable for the store and Vault hops given the drivers in use, and whether the IDE, tray and apiclient fall inside the requirement's scope. _(was 7/10 · 7/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **12.3.5** (L3) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb asks for strong, PKI-based, replay-resistant authentication verifying each endpoint of an intra-service hop. The engine's only setting named for it, `proxy_intra_service_auth: Literal[...] = "none"` at `messagefoundry/config/settings.py:771`, is read in exactly one place -- `return self.proxy_intra_service_auth != "none"` at `:804` -- so nothing branches on its value (verified at 166634c9).
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment an operator who declared `"mtls"` would believe the proxy-to-engine hop was mutually authenticated and it would not be: a control that reports itself on while doing nothing. The hops themselves would be authenticated by static bearer tokens, a SQL password and a Vault token.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that services communicating internally within a system (intra-service communications) use strong authentication to ensure that each endpoint is verified. Strong authentication methods, such as TLS client authentication, must be employed to ensure identity, using public-key infrastructure and mechanisms that are resistant to replay attacks."

**What holds it short today.** Every intra-service authenticator on shipped defaults fails at least two of the three named properties. The opaque session token is high-entropy and server-side revocable, which is a real design virtue, but revocability is not replay resistance: it is a static secret replayed verbatim on every request. Neither DB backend calls `load_cert_chain`, so the engine never presents a certificate to its own store, and Vault gets a bearer token with no engine-supplied SSLContext. The cert-identity plane that does exist is fenced to a single route.

**The research question.** What would an honest pass require on a product whose multi-process and multi-node coordination is store-mediated by design, so there are few intra-service hops and the store hop inherits the entire coordination trust burden? Name the unknowns: whether an attestation-only setting should exist at all or whether it can be made to verify something; whether mutual PKI is reachable for the store and Vault hops given the drivers in use; and whether the requirement's "services" reading pulls in the IDE extension, tray and apiclient, or excludes them as clients. The exclusion is worth pricing precisely because it is the more permissive outcome.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Defaulting `proxy_intra_service_auth` to `"mtls"` while no code reads it -- that is the exact shape this cell exists to catch, and it would convert a recorded gap into a false claim. Nor is re-declaring the cell `na` on the grounds that the remaining peers are clients rather than services: that removes the cell from the denominator without earning a Level 3 claim, which is a scope re-declaration dodging the verb.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. NO HONEST PATH TO `pass` EXISTS on the declared scope, and recording that is the deliverable -- but the residual it would rest on is at least three hops short, and both adversarial passes found the same ones independently.** Every factual sentence in this item holds at HEAD `79fdfe2b` and each was re-measured rather than inherited: `proxy_intra_service_auth` ships `"none"` (`config/settings.py:817`) with exactly one read, `return self.proxy_intra_service_auth != "none"` at `:850`, and NOTHING branches on WHICH value is set (zero hits for a value comparison across six trees, against a live positive control of 14 for a setting that IS branched on); neither store backend calls `load_cert_chain` (zero in `messagefoundry/store/`, positive control nine such sites elsewhere in the engine); Vault gets a bearer with no engine-supplied context; and the certificate-identity plane has exactly one consumer in the whole API (`api/app.py:4849`).

**The blocking limb, named exactly, is public-key infrastructure conjoined with mutuality on ONE hop: engine to the SQL Server store.** `store/sqlserver.py:1594-1600` emits every login mechanism the driver exposes and there are exactly three -- a SQL login (fails mutuality, PKI and replay resistance), `Trusted_Connection=yes` (mutual and replay-resistant, and symmetric tickets from a key distribution centre, so it fails the PKI clause the verb names), and `Authentication=ActiveDirectoryDefault` (a replayable bearer). There is no certificate arm to add because the wire protocol has no place to put one. **The one hole a hostile assessor would reach for is closed here:** the directory-token arm runs a credential chain that CAN be seeded by a client certificate, so it looks as though the hop could be certificate-authenticated. Grant the premise entirely and it still fails, on the limb decomposition rather than on the driver -- a certificate in that position authenticates the engine to the identity provider, on a DIFFERENT hop, and what is presented ON the store hop is a bearer, one-way and replayable within its lifetime. And one hop is enough: the coverage limb is the partial rule's second clause, and the method's own worked example grades a sibling cell partial for two connectors that cannot speak TLS in ANY configuration even though they exist only when an operator configures them.

**The refuse-to-start route collapses twice, and the second reason is independent of the store.** Such a gate has two honest shapes: refuse the SQL Server backend outright, which closes the cell by deleting the flagship enterprise backend and is buying the verdict with the product's purpose; or carry an exemption arm, which the record already rules is never a pass. Independently, the same gate would refuse a stock `serve` on a laptop before that backend is in the picture -- the local hops are the tray (`tray/probe.py:127-129` states it never carries an Authorization header, so it presents nothing at all by design), the bearer-authenticated apiclient consumers, and any scraper on the metrics route, over a single cleartext loopback listener. So the startup-refusal limb reduces to the shipped-default limb plus the store blocker.

**Three hops are missing, and the convergence is the point.** Two of them are rows the record's own table already enumerates. Engine to OIDC identity provider: `auth/oidc/flow.py:259-260` posts a static `client_secret`, or omits it for a public client relying on a code challenge, over a context verifying only the far end. Engine to AI broker: `transports/ai_broker.py:197` sends a static `x-api-key`, and the module's own docstring says the target is a customer-managed or self-hosted endpoint, which makes it internal by construction, with only a host allow-list as a peer control -- the same non-authenticator class this analysis correctly disposes of for the proxy trusted-list and the client-network gate. Engine to webhook alert receiver: `pipeline/alert_sinks.py:350-353` posts with a content-type header and NO credential of any kind, and `AlertsSettings` (`config/settings.py:2874-2879`) declares only a URL, a timeout and an allowed-hosts list, so there is nowhere to put one. **Consequence for the deliverable:** the residual sentence "every intra-service hop is mutually PKI-authenticated except the store login" would be FALSE in shipped code even after every proposed item landed, so it must name the protocol-level blocker as the one durable wall and say that AT LEAST three further hops remain on static secrets. The same pass surfaced the mechanism most on-verb and never named in the build costing: `transports/signing.py` plus `transports/smart.py:208,:226` already mint asymmetric, replay-resistant client assertions with a unique identifier and a short expiry for the SMART path, which makes the identity-provider arm the cheapest genuine win on the board rather than merely a missing row.

**Still not an honest pass:** this item's two traps hold, and the second has gained a stronger reason -- re-declaring the cell `na` buys nothing, because the current standard dropped the earlier clause letting a documented exclusion preserve a compliance claim. One correction the next reader should not inherit: the cell's own hostile-attack paragraph quotes a phrase as if it were this requirement's text, and it is a sibling requirement's wording; the cell wins on the pinned text anyway and the misquote should be fixed in the same citation refresh. Five more that would look like progress: counting Windows Integrated authentication as satisfying the PKI clause (mutual, replay-resistant, and symmetric tickets -- the certificate extension touches only the client's bootstrap, is not the default, and is not something the engine configures or can observe); counting a certificate-seeded directory token as certificate authentication to the store; building the pre-shared header check and treating the hop as authenticated (worth building, because it removes a control that reports itself on while doing nothing, and a pre-shared header can never satisfy PKI or replay resistance); shipping a startup gate with an attested-exemption arm and citing it as the refusal limb; and citing `[api].trusted_proxies` or `[security].allowed_client_networks` as the authenticator, since the first decides whose forwarded-for header is believed and rejects no connection while the second is a source-address gate in middleware. One instrument condition: making code branch on the proxy attestation's value would make the cell's own machine-checkable absence claim start matching, at exactly the moment a triggered re-verification makes the cheap flip most tempting, so the successor absence claim must be specified in the same change. Proposed work, unallocated and by subject: the proxy-hop attestation-to-enforcement conversion, landing with the runbook edit that currently tells operators the network value is correct; a Postgres store-hop client certificate against a `cert` authentication method (noting `config/settings.py:605-609` currently tells operators that backend has no non-static identity mode, which must move in the same change); the Vault client certificate across all three construction sites; the IDE client-certificate option, the only declared artifact with no certificate path in any configuration; the tray probe client certificate, which does not violate its deliberately tokenless boundary; a first-party consumer for the apiclient's built-but-unconsumed certificate parameter, worth doing alongside the tray and IDE work and explicitly not alone; the OIDC client-assertion arm reusing the shipped assertion signer; an AI-broker client certificate and a webhook-sink authentication mechanism, since a credential-less POST to an internal receiver would be wrong in shipped code regardless of the verdict; the AD bind non-static arm and the SMTP relay client certificate, closing the optional-authentication hole where an anonymous relay means the engine authenticates with nothing; requiring a verified, mutually-authenticated syslog hop when forwarding is on, removing the attested arm as part of the work; settling the store-protocol certificate question once with one vendor documentation citation at a named driver version plus one negative connection attempt on the existing SQL Server CI leg, and pinning it in the cell -- the cheapest item on the list and the one the whole ceiling rests on; the citation refresh at its measured non-uniform offsets, explicitly not by a mechanical offset; and the risk-register wording correction from a diffuse three-hop description to the single protocol-level blocker plus the buildable-and-unbuilt list.

## 1182. research an honest pass for ASVS 13.2.1 -- backend hops where no individual-account credential exists in any configuration

Value 7 for a real gap with no compliant option available to an operator on five of the hops; difficulty 7 because the research must price five separate missing mechanisms (LDAP SIMPLE bind, SMTP XOAUTH2, Vault AppRole and lease renewal, OIDC client_secret, and the Postgres validator that rejects anything but sql auth) against an owner decision on per-backend scoping the item is forbidden to pre-empt. _(was 7/10 · 7/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **13.2.1** (L2) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb asks that backend component communications authenticate with individual service accounts, short-term tokens or certificates, and not with unchanging credentials. The store hop ships `auth = SqlAuth.SQL` -- a static username plus a password brace-quoted into the ODBC DSN -- and the gate that would refuse it, `require_managed_identity: bool = False` at `messagefoundry/config/settings.py:488`, ships off (verified at 166634c9).
> Verdict: research
