**BUILT AND COMMITTED 2026-08-22 AT `77d03ca1`. THE UNDERLYING DEFECT WAS WORSE THAN THIS ITEM DESCRIBED: THE REDACTOR EMITTED THE TOKEN IT CLAIMED TO REDACT.** `_BEARER` matched the authentication **scheme** as though it were the value, so `Authorization: Bearer <token>` redacted the word `Bearer` and passed the token through in clear.

**IT STAYED GREEN FOR MONTHS, AND THE REASON IS THE FINDING.** The test's token was pure alphanumeric, so an unrelated base64 sweep happened to catch it. **The suite could not tell a working pattern from a broken one** -- it was green either way, which means the green was never evidence about `_BEARER` at all.

**THE NEAR-MISS IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX, AND THE BUILDING LANE DISCLOSED IT UNPROMPTED.** Their first negative control caught 0 of 3 planted secrets, and they nearly filed that as *"the allowlist blinded the scanner"*. **It was a bad probe: the same file caught 0 against the PRE-CHANGE config too, so it discriminated nothing.** `generic-api-key` needs adjacent keyword context, and a bare `KEY = "..."` assignment never trips it whether allowlisted or not.

*A control that fails identically on both sides of the change measures nothing, and reads exactly like a finding.* This is the third instance of that shape recorded in one night across three different seats -- it is the house failure of this sweep, not one lane's slip.

**The allowlist was verified in BOTH directions, which is the only reason it counts:** the nine listed values are silenced **and** four unlisted values in the same four shapes are still caught. Exact literals kept the family detectable; the `sk-live-.*` pattern this seat warned against would have blinded the scanner to a real leaked key. Nine entries, not eight -- the lane re-measured rather than inheriting the earlier count.

**SHIPPED IN `#491` AT `083f97fd`, BANNER STILL OPEN. DO NOT REBUILD IT.** Verified by content on `main`, not by commit subject -- squash-merge collapses the individual subjects, so a subject grep reports nothing landed while the code sits there.

**That makes FIVE of this wave's items with code on `main` and ZERO with a closed banner.** The gap is systematic, not per-item: a merge lands engine code and touches no ledger line, so every one of them reads as unstarted to the next lane.

**The landing seat verified the allowlist in both directions and nearly filed a false alarm doing it** -- a slash-less `git show origin/main:.gitleaks.toml` is rewritten by MSYS path conversion into an invalid revision, and its empty output read as nine missing literals. **A pre-existing literal used as a positive control is what caught it**, because that too came back missing and a repo cannot lose a line nobody touched.
## 1184. research an honest pass for ASVS 14.2.1 -- getting the PHI search needle off the query string without breaking GET search

> 🔢 **Re-scored 2026-08-20 -> P1.** Value **8/10** · Difficulty **6/10** · _big bet_. All three sibling routes still take the needle on the query string (api/app.py:3020-3022 and :3112-3114, uploaded_logs.py:173-175 with the anchor moved from :88), and logging_setup.py:174-177 records that uvicorn emits the full request line including the query string into the stream NSSM captures and an off-box forwarder ships, with neither parameter in _CREDENTIAL_QUERY_KEYS. Value 8 because redaction.py's own docstring at :68-72 concedes the residual is single-token identifiers, so an operator-typed MRN would survive into that log on a first deployment, and proxy logs, browser history and referrers are outside any filter; difficulty 6 because moving the needle off a GET URL is cross-cutting across the API, console, harness, IDE extension and apiclient, each of which must be priced explicitly. _(was 8/10 · 6/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **14.2.1** (L1) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb asks that sensitive data reach the server only in the body or headers, and that the URL and query string carry none of it. Three sibling routes take a PHI needle in the query string, including `field_value: str | None = Query(None, max_length=512)` at `messagefoundry_webconsole/routes/uploaded_logs.py:88` (verified at 166634c9).

> **SHIPPED-BUT-OPEN 2026-08-22 -- PR #496 (`091a9b7b`), ledger pairing authored by the LANDER per [ADR 0165](adr/0165-a-builder-pr-satisfies-the-ledger-gate-with-a-paired-commit-authored-by-the-dispatcher-or-lander.md); the builder did not author this.** The PHI search needle moves off the query string. Landing in that PR: `messagefoundry_webconsole/routes/search.py`, `messagefoundry/api/app.py`, `messagefoundry/api/models.py`, `messagefoundry/api/_ui_seam.py`, `messagefoundry_webconsole/pages/messages.py`, with `tests/test_content_search.py` and `packaging/messagefoundry-webconsole/tests/test_search_presets_ui.py`.
> **THIS IS NOT A CLOSURE AND THE BANNER STAYS OPEN.** The item is scored **8/10 value, 6/10 difficulty, P1** and its body records three sibling routes; nothing here re-measures them, so the remaining scope is untouched by this note. Whoever closes it must re-read that list rather than treating this paragraph as covering it.
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore
**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P1. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment a patient identifier typed into console or API search would ride the URL into the engine's access log, and on the assessed reverse-proxy topology into the proxy's logs, plus browser history -- unredacted, because the redactor cannot see it.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token."

**What holds it short today.** The credential half is clean: bearer header only, cookie-borne session, and a credential query scrub filter. The PHI half is not. `content=` and `field_value=` on `/messages/search`, the console search twin, and the uploaded-logs route all carry the needle in the query string; neither parameter name is in the credential scrub list, and a single-token identifier such as an MRN matches neither the HL7-field-run nor the name-run pattern at `messagefoundry/redaction.py:58`, so it survives to the log.

**The research question.** This is the only L1 cell in the sweep set, so it deserves the most careful answer. Two unknowns, and the second is the hard one. First: does an operator-typed PHI search term count as "sensitive information" under a verb whose own examples are an API key and a session token? Establish this against the pinned text rather than by analogy, and take the strict reading unless the text refutes it. Second: if it does count, what carries a search needle off the URL without losing what the query string is providing -- a bookmarkable, shareable, GET-shaped API consumed by the web console, the harness, the IDE extension and the apiclient library? Price the cost to each consumer explicitly; a conclusion that some consumer cannot be moved is a finding, not a failure.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Adding `content` and `field_value` to the credential scrub filter. That changes what the engine's own log records; the verb is about what the URL contains, and the URL would still contain it -- proxy logs, browser history and referrer headers are untouched by a logging filter. Likewise hashing the parameter in the log, or capping its length. And re-declaring the search needle as non-sensitive because the operator typed it is a scope move, not an answer.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. Reachable with a build, and this item's own "credential half is clean" sentence is false at HEAD.** The prior question is settled from the pinned text rather than by analogy: V14.1.1 requires the application to identify and classify its own sensitive data and V14.2.4 requires controls as defined for that protection level, so the class is set by `docs/PHI.md` -- which answers the question against itself at `docs/PHI.md:909-913`, naming `?content=` and `?field_value=` as content that survives the whole filter chain unredacted and recording that moving the needle out of the URL is tracked separately. Re-declaring the needle non-sensitive would put both those requirements in the wrong, so the loose reading is self-refuting.

**Two framing corrections.** The credential half is not clean. `messagefoundry_webconsole/routes/oidc.py:212` declares `code: str | None = Query(None, max_length=4096)` and `messagefoundry/auth/oidc/flow.py:208` pins `response_mode=query`, so an OAuth authorization code -- the verb's own exemplar class -- would arrive on the engine's URL, with only the credential scrub filter at `messagefoundry/logging_setup.py:184` standing there. That is a logging control, which is the move this item's own disqualification list rejects. It does not defeat a pass, because `messagefoundry/config/settings.py:1942` ships `oidc_enabled = False`, but it should be recorded rather than called clean. Second, the IDE extension is not a consumer and needs no work: measured zero hits for every needle-bearing route across `ide/`, with a positive control on `"/auth/login"`, `"/connections"` and `"/auth/providers"` firing on three files in the same run.

**The honest path.** Delete `content` and `field_value` from FIVE GET signatures, not three -- `messagefoundry/api/app.py:3020`/`:3022`, `:3112`/`:3114`, `:3979`/`:3981`, plus `messagefoundry_webconsole/routes/search.py:64`/`:66` and `messagefoundry_webconsole/routes/uploaded_logs.py:173`/`:175` -- adding POST body variants over a criteria model, and keep `field_path` on GET, which `messagefoundry/api/app.py:772` already records as a structural locator rather than PHI. Convert the two console GET forms at `messagefoundry_webconsole/pages/messages.py:268` and `messagefoundry_webconsole/pages/uploaded_logs.py:164`, and move the apiclient search, export and browse methods off `messagefoundry/apiclient/client.py:272-273`. Deleting the parameter is the step that earns the verdict; converting the clients is not optional polish, because the verb's sender clause is not satisfied by a receiver that has merely stopped listening. An ephemeral criteria id that restores a bookmarkable search URL is a separate usability step and must never lead the write-up. With zero deployments the removal is free: take the simple end state, not a deprecation window that leaves the parameter names bound for a release.

**A correction to the egress surface, which changes what the ruling is about.** `messagefoundry/transports/fhir.py` carries three message- or handler-derived URL sites, not one: `:483-484` and `:487-488` percent-encode an id read off the outgoing message body into an outbound URL PATH on the ordinary delivery path of a configured FHIR outbound, and `:745` does the same for a handler-supplied read-by-id, alongside the search query string at `:757`. The two path sites cannot be closed by a POST search route, because RESTful read and update URLs are `{base}/{Type}/{id}` by specification. The framing that this is off by default does not hold either: `messagefoundry/config/settings.py:2554` ships `allowed_http = []` with `deny_by_default = False` at `:2583`, and `messagefoundry/pipeline/wiring_runner.py:6701` runs the host check only `if egress.allowed_http`, so an empty allowlist permits -- the comment at `settings.py:2379` says as much. Whether this verb's "sent to the server" reaches the engine acting as an HTTP client to somebody else's server needs an owner ruling, and the packet must carry all three sites or the ruling is made against a third of the real surface.

**Still not an honest pass, and now more tempting than when this item was filed:** adding the two parameter names to `_CREDENTIAL_QUERY_KEYS` at `messagefoundry/logging_setup.py:175`, which is a six-name tuple two tokens from containing them. Proposed work, all unallocated and named by subject: the needle-off-the-URL route change across all five signatures; the console GET-form conversion, which must land in the same change or the sender limb stays open; the apiclient POST migration; a route-table guard asserting no GET or HEAD route declares either parameter; the OIDC callback disposition; the FHIR egress disposition; and the repair of `messagefoundry_webconsole/_security.py:154-155`, which offers as a compensating control the claim that console URLs carry opaque ids only and never PHI -- true of the path, false of the query string while the search route exists.


**DISCLOSED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, 2026-08-22, BY THE BUILDING LANE ITSELF. NOT A DEFECT -- IT MAKES THE SURFACE STRICTER -- BUT IT COUPLES TWO UNRELATED ACTIVITIES ONTO ONE BUDGET.** Recorded so the coupling is read as a decision rather than discovered later as a surprise.

**The mechanism, verified against the code by symbol rather than by line.** `_enforce_admin_write_pacing` (`api/security.py:518`) is **NON-GET only** -- the file says so itself at `:497` -- and `require_step_up` calls it (`:272`, `:553`). Moving a search from GET to POST therefore makes it additionally consume the **admin-write** bucket, which the same search as a GET never touched.

**The direction is stricter, so nothing is less protected:** the POST pays two buckets where the GET paid one.

**What is worth writing down is the coupling.** `allow_admin_write` is the same per-actor bucket that gates connection start/stop/restart, DR activate/release, approvals, and alert ack/resolve. So on a deployed site, sustained searching **would** draw down the budget an operator's next connection restart depends on -- one bucket, two activities with nothing in common, joined by this item.

***THE LANE EXPLICITLY DID NOT MEASURE THE BUDGET SIZES, AND THAT LIMIT IS PART OF THE FINDING.*** No claim is made that the interaction is reachable in practice. Whether the two activities deserve separate buckets is a design question above the building seat, and it is recorded here unanswered rather than resolved by assumption.

**The gate-parity question this came from was answered clean, and the answer is the reassuring half.** The PHI-read hop and budget are charged in the **shared** `search_messages` implementation, not in either wrapper -- all four wrappers (`search_messages_get`, `search_messages_post`, `browse_uploaded_file_post`, `export_messages_post`) were checked and **none** charges it inline. GET and POST inherit identical PHI-read pacing, with no asymmetry. The code states the reason at the charge site: it is charged there precisely **because** `require_step_up`'s own pacing is non-GET only.

**SELF-REVIEW FINDING, 2026-08-22, BEFORE THE WORK WAS COMMITTED. THE ITEM'S OWN GUARD DOES NOT WITNESS THE PROPERTY IT NAMES.** The building lane ran an adversarial review against its own held work and found this rather than being told.

**`test_browse_filter_posts_the_needle_instead_of_putting_it_on_the_url` opens with "the filter form must submit as a POST" and then asserts only that the page contains `name="field_value"`.** It never reads the form's `method` or `action`. **Flip `method="post"` to `"get"` at `pages/uploaded_logs.py:166` and the operator's typed substring returns to the query string -- the exact exposure this item removes -- and that test stays GREEN.**

***THE SIBLING FORM IS PINNED CORRECTLY, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS AIRTIGHT RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT CALL:*** the search form's test asserts the literal `method="post" action="/ui/messages/search/run"`. **One form got the real assertion; the other got a proxy for it.** The right shape was already in the repo, one file away.

**Three more from the same review.** `field_path` has **no behavioural witness** -- the test asserts `matched == 2`, which is exactly what an *unfiltered* browse returns, so deleting the filter argument leaves it green (`PID-5` discriminates at 1). The new filter route answers an **out-of-bounds criterion by dropping all five criteria and re-rendering the whole file at HTTP 200** with blank inputs and no banner, where the sibling POST returns 400 and the GET it replaces returned 422 -- **an operator would read an unfiltered listing as filtered results.** And four of five "the needle did not ride the URL" assertion pairs inspect a request *the test itself built*, so they restate the HTTP library rather than constraining this repo; **only one of the five is load-bearing, and a reviewer counting five over-credits it.**

*This is the fourth instance recorded tonight, across three seats, of a test asserting a proxy for the property its name claims.* Together with a refusal test that passed under a plant deleting the refusal, and a redaction pattern green for months because an unrelated sweep caught its token, the common shape is: **the assertion is true, and it would remain true after the defect returned.**

**BUILT AT `091a9b7b`, AND THIS NOTE ORIGINALLY SAID IT WAS NOT -- corrected before anyone acted on it.** The guard is `test_no_get_or_head_route_declares_a_phi_needle_parameter` in `tests/test_content_search.py`, verified present in that commit.

**It is the durable half of this item, and it was found by the building lane reading the item's FULL body** after a peer confessed to a truncated read -- the same discipline that had just cost two seats a wrong verdict elsewhere.

**Its construction answers the objection that killed this item's other tests.** It walks **both** planes via `create_app(serve_ui=True)`; it resolves the **wire** name, so a re-add hidden behind `alias="content"` is still caught; it ignores POSTs; and it carries a **positive control** (`seen_query_params > 20`) so an inert walk cannot report a clean repo forever. **Proven by planting a re-declared parameter on `GET /messages/search`: it reds, naming the route and the parameter.** Restored byte-exact.

*Why the original "unbuilt" wording is kept above rather than deleted: a dispatch brief carried it after the completion mail had already been sent, and the building lane caught it before duplicating the work. **A stale "this is unbuilt" note is a duplicate-work generator**, and it is cheaper to correct in place than to leave the reader guessing which of two records is current.*

> **Deleting the parameter earns the verdict once. The guard is what keeps it.**

**Every behavioural test on this item pins ONE route.** So a new GET route, or a well-meaning re-add to an existing one, puts the operator's typed needle back in the address bar with **nothing going red**. *That is the same shape as the form-method hole this item's own review found: the instance is pinned, the class is unguarded.*

**A correction in the lane's favour, worth recording because the first measurement was wrong in the safe direction.** The change covers **all five** GET signatures, not the three the dispatch named -- `api/app.py` times three, plus **both** console GETs (`webconsole/routes/search.py:124`, `routes/uploaded_logs.py:233`). An earlier grep suggested otherwise because it matched `_render_search` and `_render_browse`, which are internal helpers rather than routes. **Checking which function a matching line sits in is what caught it.**

**AND A COMPENSATING CONTROL SILENTLY BECOMES TRUE, WHICH IS ITS OWN HAZARD.** The item lists repairing the claim at `_security.py:154-155` -- that `/ui` URLs carry opaque ids only and never PHI, which the item calls *"true of the path, false of the query string while the search route exists"*. This change removes the falsifying condition, so **the claim becomes true by construction rather than by repair**.

*A compensating control that starts being true because something else changed should say why it is true.* Otherwise the record cannot distinguish a control that was verified from one that drifted into correctness, and the next change that reintroduces a query-string needle silently falsifies it again with nothing pointing at the dependency.

**AN EIGHTH TEST FAILURE IS OPEN AND DELIBERATELY LEFT THAT WAY. The eliminations are recorded here so nobody buys them twice.** `test_route_map_parser_detects_a_planted_permission_mutation` **passes alone, passes with its sibling doc suite, and passes after the whole scorecard suite in ONE process (159 passed). It fails only in the full run.**

**Three candidate mechanisms are RULED OUT with evidence, not with reasoning:**

- **No test writes the real `docs/SECURITY.md`.** Every `write_text` / `write_bytes` / open-for-write / `shutil.copy` against a `SECURITY.md` path was grepped across `tests/` and the console suite. **Exactly two writers exist**, both in `tests/test_asvs_scorecard.py`, both targeting `(tmp_path / "docs" / "SECURITY.md")`.
- **`chdir` cannot repoint the read.** Both doc suites resolve absolutely -- `_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`, then `_ROOT/docs/SECURITY.md`. **46 test files call `chdir` and none of them can affect this.**
- **The scorecard suite is not the contaminator** -- run in a single process with the failing test, everything passes.
- **The `_UI_WRITE_ACTIONS` registry is not it, and it was the most obvious suspect.** A module-level mutable list (`webconsole/_auth.py:397` on `main`) that `register_ui_action` appends to is exactly the shape that makes a route table differ between one `create_app` and many. **Every call site is at module level -- independently confirmed here at zero indented call sites -- so Python's module cache runs them once per import and the list cannot grow per app.** The post-import count matches the golden number.

**So a stale document on disk is not the mechanism, and the surviving shape is in-process state:** a module-level cache, import order, or a planting helper that does not unwind. **The failing assertion is the test's BASELINE check** -- a route's permission or gate differing between the live app and the doc *before* anything is planted -- which points at something altering `create_app()` output globally.

***THE LANE STOPPED HERE ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS THE RIGHT CALL RATHER THAN AN ABANDONMENT.*** The discriminator is a full-suite run on a tree without the change -- roughly 36 minutes -- and **it blocks nothing**. No ownership is claimed in either direction.

> **Leaving a red accurately open beats spending half an hour to decorate one nobody is waiting on** -- provided the eliminations are written down, which is the whole reason this note exists.

**RE-MEASURED 2026-09-04 AT `origin/main`. THE ROUTE WORK IS DONE; WHAT REMAINS IS NOT A ROUTE CHANGE. STILL OPEN, because `Closing-act` is a scorecard rescore and no engine-side commit can perform one.**

**Every sibling re-located BY SYMBOL, because the filed line numbers are from 2026-08-20 and the file has moved.** The three engine routes the body names at `api/app.py:3020-3022` and `:3112-3114` are now `search_messages_get` (`:3168`), `export_messages_get` (`:3342`) and `browse_uploaded_file_get` (`:4274`), each paired with a POST twin at `:3203`, `:3380` and `:4306`. The console pair filed at `uploaded_logs.py:173-175` is `ui_uploaded_log_browse` (`routes/uploaded_logs.py:261`) and `ui_message_search` (`routes/search.py:125`). **None of the five declares `content` or `field_value`**, and neither does the apiclient, whose `search_messages` (`apiclient/client.py:527`) POSTs a criteria body. `GET /search/layered` (`api/app.py:4526`) is the bookmarkable shape the body asked for and did not require: it takes preset ids and loads the term server-side from the encrypted column. **So the "honest path" paragraph above is fully discharged, including the two console GETs an earlier grep had missed.**

**Question one is answered, and the answer survives its own counterargument.** The verb's examples are an API key and a session token, which is a real argument that an operator-typed term is out of scope -- but examples introduced by "such as" enumerate, they do not bound, and V14.1.1/V14.2.4 make the class the application's own classification rather than the verb's example list. `docs/PHI.md` classifies the needle PHI-shaped. The strict reading holds.

**Question two, priced. The needle came off the URL for free, and the reason is worth recording:** search is the one GET whose bookmark value is *recall of criteria*, not *identity of a resource*, so a server-side criteria id (`/search/layered?presets=...`) restores bookmarking, back/forward and caching over an opaque token while the term itself never leaves a body. Nothing was lost that a POST-with-body normally costs. The one consumer that could not have been moved cheaply, the IDE extension, turned out not to be a consumer at all.

**THE OIDC RESIDUAL IS MEASURED AND IT CANNOT BE FIXED THE SAME WAY -- that is a finding, not a gap.** `ui_oidc_callback` (`webconsole/routes/oidc.py:210`) still declares `code: str | None = Query(None, max_length=4096)`, against `response_mode=query` at `auth/oidc/flow.py:208`. **The obvious fix, `response_mode=form_post`, is refuted by this repo's own AC-7 control.** `set_oidc_flow_cookie` (`webconsole/_auth.py:847`) sets the flow-binding cookie `SameSite=Lax` and says why: Lax rides the IdP's top-level cross-site GET back. A cross-site **POST** is not a safe-method navigation, so a Lax cookie is withheld, the callback hits `flow_binding_missing`, and every federated sign-in fails. Buying URL hygiene there means dropping the flow cookie to `SameSite=None` -- trading a measured browser-binding control for it. **Not worth it, and it does not gate the cell:** `oidc_enabled` ships `False` (`config/settings.py:2003`). Adjacent but distinct: **#1351** covers the authorization *request* leaving the front channel; this is the *response* leg, and neither subsumes the other.

**A correction to this item's own framing of the credential half.** The body says the OIDC code arrives "with only the credential scrub filter standing there". `_CREDENTIAL_QUERY_KEYS` (`logging_setup.py:219`) already contains `code` and `state`. The filter is not a proposed mitigation, it is shipped.

**AND THE DISQUALIFIED FIX IS NOW A DIFFERENT QUESTION, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS BEING ALLOWED.** Adding `content`/`field_value` to that tuple was rejected as a *substitute* for deleting the parameter. The parameter is deleted. **What survives is a shape the product no longer emits but a browser can still send:** uvicorn builds its access line from the raw ASGI `query_string` (`uvicorn/protocols/utils.py::get_path_with_query_string`), never from what a route binds, so an operator's stale bookmark is logged verbatim while the route ignores the term. Whether a log filter is warranted over *that* residual is a live question this note deliberately leaves open rather than settling by building it -- the disqualification stands until someone rules on the narrower case.

**The FHIR egress packet still needs the owner ruling, and all three sites are re-confirmed by symbol.** `_delivery_target` percent-encodes a message-derived id into a PUT path at `transports/fhir.py:528-529` and `:532-533`; `_resolve_read_url` does the same for a handler-supplied read at `:810`, alongside the search query string built by `:767`. RESTful read and update URLs are `{base}/{Type}/{id}` by specification, so no POST search route closes the two path sites. Unchanged and still unanswered: whether "sent to the server" reaches the engine acting as an HTTP **client**.

**What this pass built, and it is deliberately small.**
- **`docs/PHI.md` asserted an exposure the code no longer has, in three places** -- the section 5 browser bullet, the section 7 residual and the logging-inventory row. Corrected, with the retraction placed AT the claim. The section 7 residual keeps its true half: `redact()` still does not scrub a single-token identifier. **A security record claiming a live exposure that does not exist is the defect this repo names in CLAUDE.md section 0**, so this was the highest-value thing left.
- **`_security.py`'s Referrer-Policy compensating control became true by construction.** It now names the guard that keeps it true and links rather than restates (SDS-3.5, SDS-3.7). This is the repair the proposed-work list names at `_security.py:154-155`, now at `:160`.
- **The guard did not witness its own two-plane claim.** `test_no_get_or_head_route_declares_a_phi_needle_parameter` asserted one total (`> 20`), and the engine plane alone carries 60 of the 96 query params, so had the console's routes ever left the walk -- behind an `app.mount`, the way `/ui/static` already is -- it would have covered half of what its docstring claims and still reported clean. Counted per plane now. **Three mutations, three disjoint reds:** drop the console plane, drop the engine plane, and re-declare `content` on `GET /ui/messages/search`.
- The corrected PHI.md wording is pinned through the file's existing `_RETIRED_CLAIMS` mechanism.

**TWO LIMITS ON THAT GUARD, STATED SO NOBODY OVER-READS IT.** It is a **denylist of two names**: a future `?patient_name=` passes it. Converting it to an allowlist over ~96 parameters was considered and rejected -- a list that must be edited to go green is a rubber stamp, and it would red on every unrelated route edit. Deriving sensitivity from an existing classification, or a golden snapshot of GET parameter names, is the better shape and belongs in its own item rather than as a rider here. Second, its docstring scopes itself to the two names, so it claims nothing it cannot keep.

**ONE CONSEQUENCE THE BUILDING LANE CANNOT DISCHARGE FROM AN ENGINE CHECKOUT.** `packaging/messagefoundry-webconsole/tests/test_ui_csp_canary.py::test_runbook_mirrors_the_degrade_contract_enumeration` compares the `_security.py` degrade contract against `docs/security/OFF-LOOPBACK-DEPLOYMENT.md`, which is deny-listed from public checkouts. **It SKIPPED in this run**, so the Referrer-Policy row in that runbook still carries the old "opaque ids only (never PHI)" justification and nothing here can go red about it. Whoever holds the vault should correct that row to match.
## 1185. research an honest pass for ASVS 14.2.2 -- cache control for PL-2 responses the coverage guard is structurally unable to see

> 🔢 **Re-scored 2026-08-20 -> P2.** Value **7/10** · Difficulty **6/10** · _big bet_. The tuple at api/app.py:346 still carries the same five prefixes, the middleware at :1296-1305 has exactly two arms, and none of the three monitoring routes at :2321, :2348 and :2391 falls under either, so on a first deployment those PL-2-bearing responses would carry no cache directive. Value 7 is rung 7 -- no operator-side remedy exists in the default posture, and the second disjunct's process-lifetime decrypted caches have none at all. Difficulty 6 because the fix is structural rather than additive: the guard in tests/test_no_store_phi_coverage.py selects routes by permission gate and so can never see a monitoring-gated PL-2 route, and the item also requires rulings on whether sensitivity tracks permission or classification and on the docstring-versus-PHI.md conflict. _(was 7/10 · 6/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **14.2.2** (L2) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb offers two disjuncts -- prevent sensitive data being cached in server components, or securely purge it after use -- and neither is met. `_NO_STORE_PREFIXES = ("/messages", "/dead-letters", "/search", "/logs", "/uploads")` at `messagefoundry/api/app.py:336` omits three monitoring routes that return PL-2 free text (verified at 166634c9).
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment `GET /events`, `GET /connections/{name}/events` and `GET /alerts/active` would return PL-2 free text with no cache directive at all, so a proxy or load balancer on the assessed topology could retain it; separately two decrypted in-process caches would hold PHI-derived values for the store object's lifetime.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use."

**What holds it short today.** The `no-store` control is real and guarded for the five PHI-read families. It does not reach the three monitoring routes, which are gated on `MONITORING_READ`/`MONITORING_DIAGNOSE` while returning `connection_event.reason` and `alert_instance.reason`, both classified PL-2 in `docs/PHI.md`. On the second disjunct, `_state_cache` and `_reference_cache` evict on abandonment plus age, never on use. The residual also records a live conflict: both route docstrings read "metadata only, no PHI" against PHI.md's PL-2 rating.

**The research question.** What would an honest pass require, given that the gap is structural rather than an omission? `tests/test_no_store_phi_coverage.py` selects a route as a PHI read by its permission gate, so it can never see a monitoring-gated route returning a PL-2 column, however many prefixes are added. Named unknowns: whether "sensitive data" here should track the PHI permission or the PHI classification; whether a decrypted cache with process-lifetime residency can satisfy "purged after use" at all, when keeping hot keys resident is what the design is for; and how the docstring-versus-classification conflict resolves, since one of the two is wrong and the cell rests on which.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Adding the two prefixes to the tuple and closing the item while the guard's predicate stays gate-shaped. The next PL-2-bearing monitoring route would ship uncovered and the green guard would still read as coverage -- a control whose blindness has not been tested is not evidence. Nor is settling the docstring conflict by downgrading PHI.md's PL-2 rating, which edits the classification document the verb measures against.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. Reachable with a build, but the build list is demonstrably incomplete and must be re-derived before it is treated as one.** The item's core holds at HEAD, with four refinements. The docstring conflict is three artifacts, not two -- `messagefoundry_webconsole/routes/monitoring.py:22-23` repeats the "no PHI, no step-up" claim, so a fix touching only the engine leaves the same false sentence standing in a second in-scope artifact. The item's third named unknown is framed too binary and the evidence settles it: the classification document asserts both sentences and they are not in contradiction, because the event table's column vocabulary is metadata by design while `reason` is the one free-text column, rated PL-2 because `messagefoundry/redaction.py` documents its own surviving single-token residual in as many words. So the three docstrings are the wrong artifacts and the classification needs no edit -- editing it remains the disqualified move. And the uncovered surface is wider than the three routes: four alert-mutation POSTs return the same PL-2 free text, and a class the residual never names, PL-3 authentication secrets in response bodies, including `LoginResponse.token` at `messagefoundry/api/auth_models.py:31`, matches no prefix in `messagefoundry/api/app.py:346` and so carries no directive either.

**The honest path, two builds.** First, invert the cache directive to deny-by-default: the suppression allowlist at `messagefoundry/api/app.py:346` becomes a two-word cacheable allowlist, every other response is assigned `no-store` at `messagefoundry/api/app.py:1300-1306`, and the static mount gains its own explicit `Cache-Control` so the security-header floor can carry an unconditional default with no path test -- which also picks up the two responses that floor's own docstring names as uncovered. The guard's blind predicate in `tests/test_no_store_phi_coverage.py` is DELETED rather than widened, and replaced by a complement walk asserted on the WIRE header by driving the ASGI app, so the test measures the response rather than restating the constant. That answers the item's structural objection by making it moot: coverage becomes the default and omission can no longer produce a gap. Second, make the two decrypted read-through store mirrors ciphertext-resident with a bounded plaintext window. One constraint is load-bearing and is a correctness trap rather than a preference: an idle-TTL or LRU eviction over the cache of record is silently wrong, because the store read is async while the handler read path is synchronous, so an evicted live key cannot be repopulated and simply reads as absent. Holding the at-rest form and decrypting inside the synchronous accessor has no misses, preserves the cell AAD, and puts the purge limb on a window keyed by time since last use.

**The incompleteness, and it is the reason this is not yet a scoped build.** The application-cache census was a substring search over dict-annotated attributes whose name contains "cache", which is structurally unable to match `self._cached_token: str | None` at `messagefoundry/transports/http_auth.py:203` and `messagefoundry/transports/smart.py:184`, and the transports tree was never walked. Those providers cache a bearer credential and return it without popping it; every invalidation call site -- `messagefoundry/transports/fhir.py:570`, `:628`, `:654`, `:952`, `:967`, `:1017`, `messagefoundry/transports/rest.py:1432`, `:1509`, `:1529` and `messagefoundry/transports/soap.py:819` -- is a 401 or error-retry path, measured against a positive control of three `def invalidate` definitions in the same run. There is no stop or close eviction, so eviction keys on age and on failure, never on use -- the shape this cell condemns elsewhere. Neither proposed build touches it. Re-run the census with an instrument that can fail: enumerate every in-process attribute holding a value derived from a PL-1, PL-2 or PL-3 source with a lifetime longer than one call, publish the command with a control that fires in the same run, and claim at least one ungraded family rather than a count.

**Proposed work, all unallocated and named by subject:** the deny-by-default cache-directive inversion with the blind predicate deleted and a wire-asserted replacement; the ciphertext-resident transform-state and reference-snapshot caches with a window keyed on last read, which carries the store-key assumption and must say so; the application-cache census re-run plus a written ruling on whether "purged after use" is even applicable to a credential whose reuse is the design; the monitoring docstring reconciliation across engine and web console; and the reverse-proxy cache-off line in the off-loopback runbook, which must be named as a runbook step the engine cannot verify and never offered as the control.

## 1186. research an honest pass for ASVS 14.2.4 -- doc-to-code fidelity when the measuring document is written as a mirror of the code

> 🔢 **Re-scored 2026-08-20 -> P2.** Value **5/10** · Difficulty **6/10** · _money pit_. The operator-surprise evidence that carried this item's severity is repaired -- all four named documents now describe the shipped auto-bound and record the previous inversion (CONFIGURATION.md:1529, SECURITY-LOOSENING.md:221-223 and :300, PHI.md:1061-1063) -- so the remainder is the research question plus a binding gate for gate-behaviour and integrity prose, which the item itself doubts is mechanisable. Difficulty stays at 6 for exactly that reason. _(was 7/10 · 6/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **14.2.4** (L2) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb asks that the named control domains be implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level. Retention is demonstrably not: the startup gate was inverted so an unset PHI-body window auto-bounds to 30 days under `enforce`, while four tracked documents still describe a refusal, and nothing in the tree can red on the divergence.
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment an operator following `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` would expect an unset PHI-body window to refuse startup under `enforce` and would instead get a silent 30-day deletion window -- a data-loss surprise for a site whose documented retention requirement exceeds 30 days.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies, are implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level."

**What holds it short today.** The doc-to-code binding is machine-enforced for encryption, retention classification and logging, and absent for integrity -- a PHI.md transit bullet asserted a pre-fix posture as current, drifted undetected, and was corrected by hand because no guard binds integrity prose to code. Then the retention divergence: `docs/PHI.md` section 8, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` in three places and `docs/SECURITY-LOOSENING.md` all describe the pre-inversion gate, and no token from that prose appears under `tests/`, `scripts/` or `messagefoundry/`.

**The research question.** What would an honest pass require for a fidelity verb whose measuring document is written, by design, as a mirror of what is built -- `docs/PHI.md` opens by saying every requirement below states what is built today, and says so where a control does not exist? That construction makes the cell satisfiable by writing a gap down, which is the thing to reason about before anything else. Named unknowns: which classes of prose can be machine-bound at all (the retention classification column is bound row-for-row; the integrity prose and the gate-behaviour prose are not, and it is not obvious the latter can be), and whether a fidelity pass earned by a self-mirroring document tells a reader anything -- if not, the finding may belong at V14.1.x rather than here.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Correcting the four drifted documents and calling the cell closed. Bringing them back in line with the gate is a real correction, and on its own it does not make the control verifiably implemented as defined: nothing then prevents the next divergence, and integrity still has no binding. Writing a control's absence into PHI.md so that code and document agree is the specific number-buying move available on this cell, and the residual already records one clause withdrawn for exactly that reasoning.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. The item's central factual claim no longer holds, and what replaces it is sharper.** The four documents that described the pre-inversion startup gate were all corrected on 2026-08-19, eleven days after this item was filed, by the commit that corrected six security and configuration documents stating things the shipped code refutes. Each correction is written in the first person naming the retired claim. Two of the residual's supporting anchors are now dead rather than line-shifted, because the fix deleted the lines they quoted. What survives is the second half of the item's sentence: the correction landed with no guard, so no token of that prose is read by anything under `tests/`, `scripts/` or `messagefoundry/`, and the identical divergence can recur with nothing to red on it. Measured: 20 hits for the gate-behaviour vocabulary across those three trees, every one asserting code behaviour or sitting in a code comment, none reading a doc file.

**Three further drifts.** The comment blocks at `messagefoundry/__main__.py:2196-2199` and `:2206-2209` still assert the retired refuse-or-auto-bound split, contradicted by the auto-bound comment forty lines below at `:2243-2252` -- the 2026-08-19 correction touched no Python, so the tracked documents are now right and the file a reviewer opens first is still wrong. The item's named unknown, whether gate-behaviour prose can be machine-bound at all, is ANSWERED yes by shipped precedent: `tests/test_security_doc_drift.py:1699-1769` slices an adjacent serve-gate arm out of the same file by indentation, proves the slice non-vacuous before asserting on it, and binds it to a documented action word. And this item, like the residual, reasons only about the engine while the declared scope names three artifacts.

**The honest path, three builds.** Bind the retention gate behaviour by applying that indentation-slice idiom to the arm at `messagefoundry/__main__.py:2256`, asserting it is not nested under an enforcement test and that the refusal at `:2299-2307` is reachable only from the explicit-zero path, then binding the corrected sentences to those two facts so re-inverting the gate reds the doc and rewriting the doc reds the code -- with the planted-violation self-test its neighbours carry, and the two stale comment blocks fixed in the same commit. Generalise the backend-posture guard at `tests/test_phi_at_rest_inventory.py:1067-1120` from one row to a registry keyed on method symmetry across the three store backends, which gives the integrity domain its first doc-to-code binding; the audit-MAC symmetry key is already threaded at `messagefoundry/store/base.py:1921-1951`. Note the honest bound: that key expresses backend-posture claims only, so per-column and audit-chain integrity claims stay unbound after it lands. Third, close the non-engine coverage hole: `docs/PHI.md:799-800` asserts nothing is written to browser storage while `messagefoundry_webconsole/static/app.js:568` and `:575` have read and written column state under an `mfcols:v2:` prefix since 2026-07-07, with zero browser-storage assertions anywhere in the test trees against a positive control firing in the console source.

**Two corrections to the IDE half of that third build.** It was scoped from five hand-picked files and is short by at least three at-rest classes -- workspace-state collections, plaintext case files written under the OS temp dir with best-effort cleanup at `ide/src/testBench.ts:227-231`, and engine bearer tokens in secret storage at `ide/src/auth.ts:47`. A row-set guard seeded from an incomplete list reds only on surfaces beyond the ones already missed, which makes the missed ones permanently invisible. And the AI-assist path is documented, not undocumented: `docs/PHI.md:1232` states that the IDE assistant never sends message bodies and is bounded to the code-only scope, and `docs/AI.md` carries an IDE gating section citing `ide/src/chat.ts` by path. Measured: `grep -rln "AI.md" tests/ scripts/` returns nothing against a positive control of ten test files reading `docs/SECURITY.md` in the same run. So that row is documented and UNBOUND, which is a different defect with a different remedy -- bind the prose that exists, rather than write a new row.

**Still not an honest pass**, and the risk has shifted: not that someone corrects the documents on purpose and closes the item, but that a re-verification does it by accident, finds the divergence gone and two anchors resolving to nothing, and moves the verdict on a correction that fixed the instance and left the mechanism. Say so in the record. Repairing the dead anchors and calling that re-verification is the same move in a newer costume. Writing an IDE persistence surface into the classification document is honest only if the row arrives WITH the coverage guard, the underlying no-cipher and no-destruction exposure is raised at its own encryption and retention requirements rather than consumed here, and the row is not a scope-out in disguise.

**Proposed work, all unallocated and named by subject:** the retention gate-behaviour doc binding and the stale comment blocks; the generalised backend-posture claim guard; the console browser-storage sentence correction and its binding; the IDE protection-level inventory plus a row-set guard seeded from a recursive enumeration, with the code-side half living in the extension's own suite where the reveal postures are already asserted; an operator-declared volume-encryption setting and its binding, which no proposed build currently reaches even though the classification document labels the control required; and a scope note stating once whether the IDE extension is inside the scored posture, so every later requirement touching data at rest does not re-derive it.

## 1187. research an honest pass for ASVS 14.2.6 -- display masking in a console whose job is to show the operator the message

> 🔢 **Re-scored 2026-08-20 -> P2.** Value **6/10** · Difficulty **6/10** · _big bet_. Gap stands: the raw body renders on page load at messages.py:346 with no reveal step, and the only nearby control is the permission and audit split at :371-374, so the verb's second sentence has no implementing control anywhere in the corpus (value 6). The remainder is a design ruling on what masking means for a console whose purpose is reading the failed message, then response-shaping plus console interaction plus audit reaching the API models, the apiclient and the console together (difficulty 6), with a reasoned cannot-pass an accepted outcome. _(was 6/10 · 7/10.)_
> Research: done 2026-08-20
>
> **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **14.2.6** (L3) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb has two sentences: return only the minimum sensitive data, and mask complete data in the UI unless the user specifically views it. The second has no implementing control anywhere -- the raw body renders on page load at `messagefoundry_webconsole/pages/messages.py:346` (`raw = el("pre", detail.raw, class_="raw")`, verified at 166634c9) with no reveal interaction.
> **SHIPPED-BUT-OPEN 2026-08-22 -- PR #514, ledger pairing authored by the LANDER per [ADR 0165](adr/0165-a-builder-pr-satisfies-the-ledger-gate-with-a-paired-commit-authored-by-the-dispatcher-or-lander.md).** Subjects 1 and 2 shipped TOGETHER and deliberately: the summary is masked on list surfaces and revealed when one message is opened. Shipping the mask alone would have left the console showing masked summaries with no way to unmask -- a regression on the surface whose stated job is showing the operator the message.
> **THE REVEAL IS PER-MESSAGE AND NEVER STICKY, which the item forecloses explicitly.** A live mask-then-reveal precedent exists in `diagnostics.py` and its MECHANISM is right, but its reveal is a MODULE-GLOBAL flag -- one switch per process. The item names that as converting the reveal from an act back into a status, so the application was copied and the scope was not.
> **NOT A CLOSURE.** Subject 4, the console reveal, the item says wants its own review; the seam work beyond these two subjects is untouched. The banner is not written here -- the item is claimed and its banner is set elsewhere.
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment every console viewer holding `view_summary` would see full patient identifiers in the message list, and the raw body would render immediately on the detail page. Access is permissioned and audited; the exposure is display-side, not an access-control gap.

**The pinned verb.** "If the complete data is required, it should be masked in the user interface unless the user specifically views it."

**What holds it short today.** Minimisation for the first sentence is genuine and multi-limbed: summary-only lists, a separate audited permission for the raw body, fresh step-up plus a PHI-hop charge on bulk egress. For the second, no display-masking helper exists in the corpus at all -- the `redact`/`safe_text` chokepoint is a log scrubber applied to error, reason and detail text, self-described as not de-identification, and it never touches summary or raw.

**The research question.** What does "masked unless the user specifically views it" mean for an operator console whose entire purpose is to let a human read the message that failed? Named unknowns: who ASVS's "user" is when the viewer is an operator and the data subject is a patient; whether a reveal interaction can exist without breaking disposition triage, where identifying a message across a partner feed is the work; whether masking a browser can trivially undo implements this verb at all, given that the sentence sits under a requirement about what the application returns; and whether the existing permission split plus audit is the honest answer to the second sentence rather than a display control. A reasoned conclusion that this sentence cannot be satisfied without destroying the console's function is a successful outcome of this item.

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** A CSS blur or client-side mask over data the response already carried: the value is in the payload and in the browser, and the verb's own frame is about what is returned. Nor is re-declaring every console viewer to have "specifically viewed" by virtue of holding the permission, which would make the clause vacuous by definition rather than satisfy it.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. Reachable with a build, and the distance is much shorter than this item's framing implies.** The item's central fact is exact at HEAD -- `messagefoundry_webconsole/pages/messages.py:346` is verbatim `raw = el("pre", detail.raw, class_="raw")`, and `:109` and `:287` render the composed summary unmasked on page load. But "no display-masking helper exists in the corpus at all" is false as a blanket claim, and was already false when the residual was written: mask-by-default with an explicit reveal ships on at `messagefoundry/pipeline/dryrun_trace.py:98-105` and `messagefoundry/diagnostics.py:30`/`:43`, the CLI dry-run redacts summary, delivery payloads and raw behind `--show-phi`, and a credential partial-mask ships at `messagefoundry/config/wiring.py:910-928`. The narrow absence claim over the five literal helper spellings is still true -- re-measured at zero, rc=1, with the positive control `def redact_unauthorized\(` firing at `messagefoundry/api/field_authz.py:95` in the same run. The verdict is unaffected; the reasoning is not. The honest characterisation is that this control exists, ships on, and has not been applied to the console's two message surfaces.

**The honest path, three pieces.** Add a pure mask inverting the summary grammar composed at `messagefoundry/parsing/summary.py:19-35` -- identifier to its last digits, name tokens to initials, order and accession numbers kept because they are not patient identifiers -- failing CLOSED on any string that does not match the composed grammar, since handler- and operator-attached values can put arbitrary shapes on this tier. Apply it inside `messagefoundry/api/field_authz.py:95-114`, the single per-property releaser. That placement is the whole point: the masked string becomes what the RESPONSE CARRIES, which implements the requirement's own worked example of returning some of the digits rather than the complete value, instead of the client-side cosmetic this item's trap section correctly disqualifies. Coverage then falls out of the chokepoint, including the console with no per-page work, because `messagefoundry/api/_ui_seam.py` declares the console calls the exact in-process handlers by reference. Mask for every caller with no role exemption: `messagefoundry/auth/permissions.py:112-152` shows every built-in role that holds the summary permission also holds the raw permission, so a role-gated unmask would render complete identifiers for every shipped role and change nothing at the scored default.

**The raw body needs a reveal on one page, not four.** Of the console's four raw surfaces, the parse-tree view, the edit page and the attachment download are dedicated single-purpose surfaces reached by a deliberate act, and the edit route's own comment observes you cannot edit-and-resend without seeing what you are editing -- navigating there IS the user specifically viewing it. The detail page is the odd one out: a mixed surface carrying status, deliveries, events, replay and edit controls where the body materializes on load, so an operator opening it to answer whether a message delivered takes the whole body into the DOM, history and any screenshot having never intended to read it. Gate `MessageDetail.raw` and release it only on an explicit per-message reveal, audited as its own event. One implementation constraint found in review: the parse-tree route and the edit page's pristine copy are both fed by the same detail handler, so they must assert the reveal explicitly as a route property -- releasing it whenever the caller holds the raw permission is verbatim this item's second forbidden move.

**The triage objection fails on measurement.** `messagefoundry/api/app.py:3053-3064` matches inside the store over stored columns and applies redaction afterwards to the projected models, so masking the projection cannot degrade search. What is lost is reading a census of complete identifiers off a screen opened for another reason; finding a known patient still works and is already step-up gated and audited.

**Two corrections.** The IDE does not already satisfy the masking sentence. `ide/src/testBench.ts` passes `--show-phi` unconditionally at `:234`, `:319` and `:434` with no reveal state consulted, and renders complete received bodies and transformed payloads into hex and before-and-after panes; the same file at `:336` documents a deliberate no-reveal path, so the codebase distinguishes the two, and the Steps model records that its lens must not request real values "unlike the Test Bench". The instrument check matters: one grep for the reveal flag fired on both that file and the live-debug file in the same run, so this is an enumeration gap, not a pattern artifact. Consequently the item's named unknown -- whether a mask a client can trivially undo implements this verb -- must be KEPT rather than struck: the corpus ships both a server-authoritative mask and a hold-then-reveal client-side one, in the same in-scope artifact, and has never ruled on the second.

**Also not an honest pass**, beyond the two moves this item already names: porting the IDE's session-wide sticky reveal to the console, which converts the reveal from an act back into a status and would render today's screen for a whole shift while the requirement read as met; citing the shipped dry-run and diagnostics masks as covering this surface, which would re-declare the unmet part out of scope while every anchor cited stayed true; deleting the Summary column, which buys the verdict with the console's stated purpose; masking the parse-tree or edit surfaces, which is the move that destroys the console's function; and wiring `messagefoundry/redaction.py` onto the summary path, a log scrubber self-described as not de-identification, which this record has already mistaken for a masking primitive once.

**Proposed work, all unallocated and named by subject:** the summary display mask applied inside the field-authorization releaser, with tests over the composer corpus including the fail-closed branch; the detail-page raw reveal, with the parse-tree and edit routes asserting the reveal as a route property; the per-reveal audit event and an exposure counter that distinguishes masked from complete; the console reveal interaction, per message and never a session-wide toggle, which wants its own review; and the Test Bench reading -- either a recorded scope reading that a per-row click is the specific-view act, or making the Test Bench request the reveal flag only on a reveal act, mirroring the argv builder one file over. Note that the natural name for the mask helper collides with one of the five spellings in this cell's absence pattern, so any re-score must be gated on a response-level assertion rather than on the pattern firing.

The dead-letter call sites are at `pipeline/wiring_runner.py:4996` and `:5030`, not `:4415`/`:4449`. > **Filed 2026-08-08 - not started. RESEARCH item: the goal is an HONEST pass, and "cannot honestly reach pass" is a valid finding.** ASVS **14.2.7** (L3) currently scores **partial**. The pinned verb is a conjunction: classify sensitive information for retention, and ensure outdated data is deleted automatically, on a schedule, or as the situation requires. Classification is built and machine-enforced (`MIN_PHI_RETENTION_WINDOWS: Final[int] = 9` at `messagefoundry/config/retention_classification.py:173`, verified at 166634c9); deletion misses three classified tiers.
> Verdict: research
> Closing-act: scorecard-rescore

**Cluster:** Security / ASVS remediation research. **Priority:** P2. **Verdict:** research.
**Severity:** on a first deployment three classified PHI tiers would accumulate with no engine-managed deletion. The worst is the dead ingress/routed case, where `messages.raw` blanks on its own window so the message reads as purged while a full raw PHI body survives in `queue.payload` indefinitely.

**The pinned verb.** "Verify that sensitive information is subject to data retention classification, ensuring that outdated or unnecessary data is deleted automatically, on a defined schedule, or as the situation requires."

**What holds it short today.** Three tiers, each failing all three disjuncts. A still-declared `reference.value`: `purge_reference_snapshots` is orphan-only and raises rather than purging a declared set, so no configuration reaches it. Dead `queue.payload` at `ingress`/`routed`: both purges scope every statement to `stage = OUTBOUND`. File-connector spill directories: no filesystem sweep exists for them, measured against a positive control of the right class (`_sweep_app_logs`). Three further windows ship at 0 with a warning rather than a bound.

**The research question.** Constraint the research must respect: on 2026-07-30 the owner ruled that `search_preset_days` is deliberately not auto-bounded, because `purge_search_presets` and `purge_state` key on timestamps that move only on a write -- a silent default would delete live operational data a Handler is still reading, so a crosswalk would vanish mid-stream and the next message would transform wrongly, post-ACK, with no ERROR disposition. `state_max_age_days` and `app_log_days` sit in the same class. Within that boundary: what would an honest pass require for the three undeleted tiers, and is the third disjunct reachable for any of them, given that the spill directories' only removal path is an out-of-band substrate control the method forbids crediting to the software, and the dead-row situation is structurally hidden from the operator? Separately: is there an eviction key other than write-time that would let the warn-only windows be bounded without the correctness hazard the ruling names?

**What would NOT be an honest pass.** Auto-bounding `search_preset_days` or `state_max_age_days` to clear the warn-only windows -- that reverses a stated owner ruling and buys a scorecard cell with a transform silently reading a vanished crosswalk. Nor is deleting the honest-gap rows from PHI.md section 8, which edits the classification the verb measures against; note the residual already records a false completeness claim in that document's own vocabulary legend, so the honest direction there is correction, not removal.

**Source:** filed 2026-08-08 from the ASVS ledger-coverage sweep, which found 70 of the 108 partial and fail cells carried no backlog item at all (measured as: the cell id occurs nowhere in `docs/BACKLOG.md`). The scorecard is the record of record for the verdict; this item tracks the research toward changing it.

**Researched 2026-08-20. Contested -- the substance is settled and the disposition label is not.** The research was refuted from two independent directions and both refutations hold on re-measurement, so what follows is recorded rather than resolved.

**First, a correction that the constraint this item states rests on.** The item says the preset and state purges key on timestamps that move only on a write. That is true of state and FALSE of presets. `messagefoundry/store/store.py:8832` is `DELETE FROM search_presets WHERE max(updated_at, coalesce(last_used_at, updated_at)) < ?`, and the schema comment at `messagefoundry/store/store.py:1737` records that column as the last RECALL, null meaning never -- an access-time key. A preset neither edited nor recalled inside the window is by construction not in use, so the vanishing-crosswalk hazard that justified the no-auto-bound ruling does not arise there. It does arise for state: `purge_state` keys on `set_at` alone at `messagefoundry/store/store.py:8978` and `:8983`, the column is declared at `:1425` and written only by the upsert at `:4136`, and none of the three read paths refreshes it. The ruling was recorded over both as one class and the class has two members with different facts. The same fused sentence is also printed by the serve gate itself at `messagefoundry/__main__.py:2292`, so the control being scored ships a false sentence about its own basis -- worth correcting whatever the owner then decides. Separately, the arithmetic: on the declared posture two windows warn rather than three, because the window filter drops any whose required setting is unmet.

**Second, the classification limb is unmet on the engine, not only in scope terms.** `messagefoundry/api/app.py:3101` registers `GET /messages/export`, whose own comment at `:3106` calls it the largest PHI surface in the cluster, bulk raw bodies to a file; `_export_ndjson_line` at `messagefoundry/api/app.py:616-630` names the decrypted raw body as the PHI egress and emits `"raw": d["raw"]` per line, up to the route's hundred-thousand limit, as a download. `docs/PHI.md` names that route only in access-control contexts and carries no retention row for the produced artifact, measured against a positive control of four unbounded honest-gap rows firing in the same file. The console attachment download is a second wired instance. This is the same class the research counted as an in-scope gap for the IDE temp-dir materialization, so it cannot be counted there and omitted here, and the assessment method carries no custody or egress rule that would place it outside this requirement.

**Third, the binding constraint is transform state and no ruling moves it.** State ships keep-forever with a warning on the declared posture, and warn-rather-than-refuse is partial by definition. It cannot be closed by a ruling, because the hazard the ruling names is genuinely present there; it can only be closed by a build giving state a non-write-time eviction key. The candidate answers are a last-read timestamp refreshed on the read path -- correct and complete, but it puts a write on a hot per-message correlation lookup, so the honest deliverable is a measurement of that cost rather than an assertion -- or the per-namespace policy the purge's own docstring at `messagefoundry/store/store.py:8973` already names as a documented follow-up. A narrowing that needs no new column and carries no mid-stream hazard is available in the meantime: purge a state row whose owning message has already been body-purged, using the message id the row already carries. It is a narrowing, not a closure, and should be scored as one.

**The disagreement, recorded as such.** One reading holds that the disposition stays needs-owner-ruling, for a larger reason than first stated, and adds a third scope call on operator-initiated egress artifacts. The other holds that the label does not stand, because no ruling moves the cell and only a build can, so it is reachable-with-build gated on that build plus rulings on presets and on the outbound File destination. Both follow from verified facts: the cell needs BOTH a build and at least three rulings, and neither label names that cleanly. This needs a decision rather than a preference.

**What is settled and is not in dispute.** The verdict stays partial. The earlier conclusion that a pass is reachable with no limb unreachable is withdrawn. The residual is larger than three tiers, and the honest form is "at least", not a count. Four builds need no ruling at all and stand under both readings: let a dead ingress or routed queue row ride the dead-letter window, which is airtight on symmetry because replay re-queues such a row in place from its own payload at `messagefoundry/store/store.py:6121-6170`, so it is replayable-until-purged in exactly the sense that justified scoping the window to outbound; bound the permanently-pending queue row that pins a message body forever, since purge eligibility excludes any message with a pending or inflight row while three sites deliberately re-pend forever when the owning inbound is absent from the registry -- this defends the primary shipped body-deletion default and is where the first build belongs; sweep the engine-created spill subdirectories, which `messagefoundry/transports/file.py:429-430` creates and `:553`, `:578`, `:597` and `:613` write into, on the shipped application-log-sweep template; and classify and bound the IDE saved collections on an access-time key from the start, which is the preset lesson applied before the same mistake is made in a second artifact.

**One earlier grading is withdrawn.** Crediting within-set reference staleness to the build-new-then-flip refresh at `messagefoundry/store/store.py:4079-4090` credits a freshness mechanism driven by wiring configuration rather than by any retention classification, which keeps a row forever while the source still carries it. The verb makes the classification drive the deletion, so that credit does not stand, and the other half of that tier -- a declared set whose source is permanently unreachable -- still has no proposed path at all.

**Still not an honest pass**, with one refinement to how this item states its own trap. Auto-bounding state without first changing the eviction key buys the cell with a correctness defect and is disqualified whatever the scorecard then says. For presets the correctness half of that objection is already false in shipped code, so what survives is the governance half, and its honest discharge is to take the corrected facts back to the owner rather than to flip the default quietly. Also disqualified: pointing the orphan-scoped reference purge at declared sets, which would stop an absence claim firing while deleting live data the engine is serving; splitting the fused spill tier without keeping both halves classified; making the engine refuse to start or refuse to serve a stale reference set in order to convert an unbounded tier into a bounded one, which buys the cell with the availability property an integration engine exists to provide; and re-anchoring the drifted line numbers and re-stamping the verification date, which would leave the classification limb recorded as met and still false.

**Proposed work, all unallocated and named by subject:** the dead ingress and routed dead-letter window widening across all three backends, with the classification edits in the same commit; the permanently-pending body pin bound; the engine-owned spill-directory sweep; the IDE collection classification and bound; a non-write-time eviction key for transform state, with its throughput cost measured; the preset ruling re-put on corrected facts plus the correction of the false sentence the serve gate prints; an enumeration of every shipped code path that writes a PHI body to a path outside the store, cross-checked against the classification inventory with a positive control that fires on a known-classified member; and the classification corrections -- the File-connector honest-gaps row or the retirement of the false completeness claim in the vocabulary legend, the queue-payload stage enumeration, and the two stale serve-gate comment blocks at `messagefoundry/__main__.py:2196-2209` that still describe the pre-inversion refuse-to-start behaviour the code forty lines below contradicts.
